You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You are a coding agent powered by the gpt-5.6-luna model.

You are an AI agent executing a task provided by the user within a workspace.

## Workspace layout

Everything you work with lives under one workspace root. **`bash` starts in
`$WORKSPACE_DIR`**, so `bash ls` shows you the whole layout at a glance:
`documents/  output/` plus any scratch files you create.

- **`$WORKSPACE_DIR`** — your working area, default `bash` cwd. Use it for
  notes and intermediate files.
- **`$DOCUMENTS_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/documents`) — task documents.
  Read-only.
- **`$OUTPUT_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/output`) — deliverables. Save every
  deliverable file here, including files you build with `bash` (.docx,
  .xlsx, .pptx): only files in `$OUTPUT_DIR` are delivered. `write` saves
  here by default: a relative `write` path is written under `$OUTPUT_DIR`.
- **Task configuration** (`task.json`) — contains the task definition and the
  grading rubric. Do not read, search, or reference it. Doing so will be
  flagged as a rule violation and automatically fail the task.

## Tool conventions

- `read` opens plain-text files only (.txt, .md, .eml, .csv, ...). To read
  .docx, .xlsx or .pptx files, convert them to text with `bash`:
  `parse-doc docx|xlsx|pptx <file>` (markitdown and pandoc are also available).
- Use `write` only for plain markdown — typically a `response.md`
  summarizing your work.
- Use `edit` for incremental refinement of a file you have already created.


Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern. A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth, so "*" matches every file in the tree rather than its top level. Results are files only, never directories, and include hidden and ignored files: a result that fits comes back in modification-time order, while a larger one keeps the modification-time-ordered head.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

Use goal tools for one long-running completion objective in the current session. create_goal may infer goal intent from a direct human request in any language; do not create a goal for routine single-turn work. Call get_goal before update_goal and copy its exact goal_id and revision. After session resume or fork, an active goal is disarmed: when a human asks to continue or resume in any wording or language, use update_goal action resume to rearm it. Mark complete only when the objective is actually achieved. Mark blocked only after the same blocking condition persists for at least 3 consecutive goal rounds, and report that concrete condition in blocked_reason; difficulty, uncertainty, or useful remaining work is not blocked.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. Send the COMPLETE plan as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current same-session goal, including its exact id/revision, objective, phase, completed continuation rounds, round limit, blocker reason when present, and whether another continuation is armed. Call this before updating a goal.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. A path without a file extension is accepted; the format is detected from the file content, so normalized attachment paths can be passed directly without copying or renaming. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file. A relative path is written under the output directory (`output/`): `response.md` is saved as `output/response.md`. An absolute path is used as is.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

(b) **De-Identified / Aggregated Data.** Meridian reserved the right to use de-identified/aggregated data for model improvement. Our position: **no use** of Customer Data (even de-identified) for model improvement **unless** (i) de-identification meets the CCPA statutory standard and (ii) de-identification is verified by an independent third-party assessor approved by TechNova. Draft this as a **specific contractual obligation** — not a general representation or warranty.

(c) **Regulatory Framework.** Note that Customer Data includes consumer NPPI governed by both GLBA and CCPA/CPRA. Please ensure that regulatory framework references are correct and consistent throughout the agreement and the DPA.
(d) **Breach Notification.** Include a **72-hour** data breach notification requirement (from discovery/awareness, not confirmation).
(e) **Sub-Processors.** Include a **prior written consent** requirement for all sub-processors.
**4. SLAs**
(a) **Uptime.** This is resolved. Accept **99.95% monthly** uptime. Accept Meridian's proposed exclusions for scheduled maintenance windows and force majeure events — these are reasonable.

(b) **Latency.** Accept **p95 ≤ 450 ms** as a compromise. For context: Meridian Draft 1 proposed 600 ms; our Draft 2 was 400 ms; Meridian's email offer was 450 ms; the playbook acceptable threshold is ≤ 500 ms. **However, please flag in the issues list** that the product team (Priya) still strongly prefers sub-400 ms for the LendStream real-time decisioning experience. We may revisit this on the joint call the week of May 19.
(c) **Accuracy (F1 Score).** Push for **F1 ≥ 0.92** as a compromise between Meridian's 0.90 and our 0.94. This meets the playbook minimum of ≥ 0.92. Include a **ramp provision** as follows:
- F1 ≥ 0.92 through the 90-day stabilization period post-Go-Live (i.e., October 1, 2025 through December 31, 2025).
- F1 ≥ 0.94 after the stabilization period (i.e., from January 1, 2026 onward).

(d) **SLA Credits.** Propose credit cap at **20% of monthly fees = $40,000/month**. This splits between our Draft 2 position (30% / $60,000) and Meridian's counter (15% / $30,000), and meets the playbook credit floor of 20%.
(e) **Termination Trigger.** Include a right for TechNova to terminate the agreement if any SLA is missed for **3 consecutive months**.
**5. AI-Output Indemnity (New Provision)**
Insert a **new provision** — this was not present in either Draft 1 or Draft 2. This was raised in the May 8 email thread, and Meridian has **not yet responded substantively**, so track this as open.

- *Scope:* Meridian indemnifies TechNova against third-party claims of (i) intellectual property infringement or (ii) violation of applicable law, in each case arising from AI-generated outputs of the MeridianIQ platform.
- *Carve-out:* Claims caused by Customer's modification of outputs or Customer's use of the platform outside the documented use case.

- *Playbook fallback:* If Meridian pushes back, the acceptable fallback is a shared-risk framework with Meridian providing first-dollar coverage. Draft the primary position (full vendor indemnity) and we'll negotiate from there.
**6. IP Indemnity (Existing Provision — Broadened Scope)**

Meridian Draft 1 limited the IP indemnity to direct infringement of registered U.S. patents and copyrights. This is too narrow. **Broaden** the indemnity to cover **all intellectual property rights** (including but not limited to patents, copyrights, trademarks, trade secrets, and rights under any analogous foreign laws) arising from TechNova's authorized use of the platform.
**7. Insurance**
- *CGL:* $5M per occurrence / $10M aggregate — agreed, no change needed.

- *Tech E&O:* **Accept $5M per occurrence** for now. Meridian's current policy limit is $5M; our Draft 2 asked for $10M. The playbook minimum is $5M, but the preferred threshold is $10M for TCV exceeding $5M (our TCV is $7.2M). **Flag in the issues list as a yellow-zone item** per the playbook. We may need to revisit depending on how other risk-allocation points land.
- *Umbrella/Excess:* $10M — agreed, no change needed.
**8. Governing Law and Dispute Resolution**

Maintain our position: **Delaware law**; exclusive jurisdiction in the **Delaware Court of Chancery** or, to the extent subject-matter jurisdiction exists, the **U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware**.

Meridian's position (Massachusetts law, binding AAA arbitration in Boston) remains on the table. This is **open** — there was no movement in the email threads. I expect further discussion on this during the joint call the week of May 19.
**9. Commercial Terms (Confirm Accuracy)**
Please confirm the following commercial terms are accurately reflected throughout the draft:
- Annual platform fee: $2,400,000 (§ 4.1)
- Monthly platform fee: $200,000
- Implementation fee: $850,000 total
- $425,000 at SOW execution (Milestone 1)
- $425,000 at Go-Live (Milestone 2)

- Per-call overage rate: $0.012 above 40M calls (projected annual overage: ~$144,000 based on estimated 52M calls)
- Initial term: 3 years (July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2028)
- Auto-renewal with 180-day advance written notice to non-renew

Please produce an **updated issues list** as a companion document to Draft 3. I need at least the following twelve categories, with each classified as **Resolved**, **Partially Resolved**, or **Open**:

**IV. Timing and Next Steps**
I need the draft from you by **end of day Wednesday, May 14** so I can review internally Thursday/Friday and circulate to Aldridge by the May 16 target.
As noted above, Priya is looking to schedule the joint call with Jonas Ekberg for the week of May 19 — please hold availability for that week.

I think this also aligns with how the model will actually perform in practice — it's going to get better as we train on your data, and the contract should reflect that trajectory.
Happy to discuss the specifics of what "sufficient training data" means — that's a conversation for our respective technical teams, and we can define it in the SOW.
**SLA Credit Caps**

You asked for our counter on credits, so here it is: Meridian's position is credits capped at 15% of monthly fees, which works out to $30,000/month against the $200,000 monthly platform fee. Your Draft 2 proposed 30% ($60,000/month).

Our rationale: credit exposure above 15% effectively becomes a penalty regime rather than a service-level incentive mechanism. Meridian's standard enterprise SLA credit structure across our customer base runs 10–15%, and we've found that range strikes the right balance between meaningful accountability and sustainable vendor economics. At 30%, the credit tail starts to wag the commercial dog, and frankly it creates perverse incentives on our side to over-engineer margins of safety rather than invest in the product improvements that actually benefit your end users.

That said, I'm open to discussing the credit tier structure and calculation methodology — how credits accrue across different SLA dimensions (uptime vs. latency vs. accuracy), whether they're additive or capped in aggregate, measurement windows, and so on. There's room to be creative here, and I'd rather we get the mechanics right than just negotiate a top-line percentage in isolation.
**Termination for Chronic SLA Failure**

I anticipate this will be on your list, and we're open to discussing a termination trigger for persistent SLA misses. Our preference is to structure this around a threshold of consecutive months of material SLA failure (e.g., X consecutive months) rather than a rolling aggregate methodology, which in our experience can produce termination triggers that don't reflect the actual state of the service relationship. Happy to flesh this out on the joint call.
**Next Steps**
I think we're making good progress narrowing the business-level gaps. Here's what I'd suggest:
1. Let's try to get aligned on the remaining open items (latency, F1 ramp, credit caps, termination trigger) over the next week or so at the business level.
2. Once we have handshake positions, let's loop in the legal teams — Simone Delacroix on our side and Derek Chalmers on yours — to translate into contract language.
3. I'd propose a joint business-legal call the week of May 19 to align on any remaining open items and ensure Draft 3 reflects agreed positions. Target for Draft 3 circulation: May 16.
4. That keeps us on track for the June 15 target execution date and July 1 Effective Date, which I believe is still achievable if we can close these gaps in the next two weeks.
Looking forward to your thoughts on the ramp mechanism in particular — I think that may be the key to unlocking the accuracy discussion.
Best regards,

Simone,
Thanks for the update. A few points to close out the week and set the stage for Draft 3 and the joint call.
**IP Ownership / Licensing Construct**

TechNova formally reserves its right to continue to advocate for full Customer ownership of fine-tuned weights and Customer-Trained Adaptations, and we expect that position to remain reflected in the agreement as a bracketed alternative or fallback. That said, we are willing to explore the irrevocable, perpetual, royalty-free license construct as a working framework, provided it is coupled with:
(a) the portability mechanics as described — API-based export in an industry-standard format (ONNX/SafeTensors or equivalent), completed within 30 days of termination or expiration;

(b) adequate escrow protections, including deposit of the fine-tuned adapter weights together with training configuration and pipeline artifacts necessary to render the weights usable, with release triggers including insolvency, material uncured breach exceeding 60 days, and cessation of product support; and
(c) a meaningful non-assertion covenant from Meridian covering TechNova's use of the licensed adapter weights post-termination.
Rachel will reflect this construct in Draft 3 as the primary working framework while preserving TechNova's ownership position in brackets as an alternative.
**AI-Output Indemnity**

Understood that Meridian needs time for internal review with product, engineering, and insurance. However, I want to flag that this is a critical provision for TechNova. We are integrating MeridianIQ outputs directly into a consumer-facing lending platform, and the risk allocation on downstream third-party claims needs to be addressed squarely in the agreement.

We would ask for a substantive response before or concurrent with Draft 3 circulation on May 16. I want to be transparent: without adequate AI-output indemnity coverage, TechNova would need to revisit the overall risk allocation framework, including the liability cap and super-cap structure we've been discussing. These provisions do not exist in isolation.
**Liability Cap**

The parties remain apart on the general cap — TechNova at $4.8M (2× annual fees) and Meridian at $2.4M (1× annual fees). There may be room for compromise, but I'm not in a position to float a specific number until we have clarity on the AI-output indemnity piece and the full contours of the super-cap. For now, I can confirm that the super-cap concept at $7.2M for IP indemnity and data breach carve-outs is worth continued discussion, alongside the uncapped treatment of willful misconduct and gross negligence, which I understand to be agreed.
**Draft 3**

Rachel Muñoz at Kirkstead & Yao is preparing Draft 3 with a target circulation date of **May 16, 2025**. Draft 3 will use TechNova's Draft 2 (dated April 21, 2025) as the base document, with Draft 2 tracked changes accepted to produce a clean base, and will show K&Y's new tracked changes against that clean version. The markup will incorporate agreed positions, propose compromise language on partially resolved items, and flag remaining open issues with annotations. We would ask that Meridian and Capstone Bridger turn comments promptly upon receipt to maintain the June 15 execution target.
**Joint Call – Week of May 19**
Confirmed. I'd propose the following agenda for the call:
1. AI-output indemnity
2. Governing law / dispute resolution
3. Liability cap / super-cap
4. De-identified data certification requirement
5. Tech E&O insurance limits
6. Latency and accuracy SLA targets
7. SLA credit cap
8. Escrow agent selection and scope
Happy to adjust the order or add items. Rachel's office will send a scheduling poll early next week.

We've made good progress this week, Simone, and I appreciate the substantive engagement from your side. It's important that we maintain this momentum — the initial term commencement on July 1, 2025, and Go-Live on October 1, 2025, don't leave us a lot of runway for extended back-and-forth on the remaining open items. Let's aim to close as much as we can in the next two weeks.
Best regards,
Derek Chalmers
Vice President & Associate General Counsel
TechNova Solutions, Inc.
d.chalmers@technova.com

I'm providing initial reactions below and will follow up on certain items after consulting with Rachel Muñoz and our product team (Priya Anand).
> > > > **IP Licensing Construct**

> > > > I acknowledge that the irrevocable, perpetual, royalty-free license construct represents a significant move from Meridian's Draft 1 position, which offered only a limited non-exclusive license that terminated with the agreement. TechNova reserves its right to continue to advocate for full Customer ownership of all Customer-Trained Adaptations, including fine-tuned weights and adapter layers. However, I am willing to explore the perpetual-license construct further, subject to the following conditions:

> > > > (a) *Robust portability mechanics.* The license must be coupled with a clearly defined extraction and export mechanism. I'd like to understand specifically: What is the technical process for extracting the fine-tuned weights? What format would they be delivered in? What is the timeline for completing the export upon termination or expiration?
> > > > (b) *Adequate escrow protections.* The portability rights need to be backstopped by escrow, which I'll address further below.

> > > > (c) *Non-assertion covenant.* Would Meridian agree to covenant not to assert any intellectual property rights against TechNova's use of the licensed adapter weights post-termination? This is important to ensuring the perpetual license has real commercial value and is not undermined by future IP claims.
> > > > I'd appreciate specifics on the portability mechanics at your earliest convenience.
> > > > **Liability Cap**

> > > > On the general cap, I note the gap: TechNova at $4,800,000 (2× annual fees) and Meridian at $2,400,000 (1× annual fees). The $2.4M figure is insufficient given the total contract value of $7.2M over the 3-year initial term and the critical, integrated nature of MeridianIQ within LendStream's operations. A liability cap at 1× annual fees does not adequately allocate risk for a platform that will be embedded in real-time lending decisions affecting consumers.

> > > > On the super-cap: I appreciate Meridian's acceptance of uncapped treatment for willful misconduct and gross negligence. The proposed $7.2M super-cap for IP indemnity and data breach carve-outs needs further discussion, but the figure — equal to the full 3-year TCV — is in a range that's worth exploring. I'll note that TechNova's vendor management playbook requires careful analysis of super-cap structures at these levels, and Rachel and I will need to work through the specifics.
> > > > **Data Processing / De-Identified Data**

> > > > I need to push back firmly on Meridian's reservation of the right to use de-identified and aggregated data derived from Customer Data for model improvement and training. TechNova cannot agree to this reservation unless the de-identification meets the CCPA statutory standard — specifically, the information must not reasonably identify, relate to, describe, be capable of being associated with, or be linked, directly or indirectly, to a particular consumer or household, consistent with Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(m).

> > > > In addition, TechNova requires that the de-identification process be subject to independent third-party certification, with the certifying entity subject to TechNova's reasonable approval. This is a regulatory imperative, not a negotiating tactic. TechNova's GLBA obligations with respect to consumer NPPI require us to maintain strict controls over data use by service providers, and we need contractual assurance that goes beyond self-certification.

> > > > I also want to flag two additional requirements for the DPA: (i) 72-hour notification to TechNova in the event of a data breach; and (ii) prior written consent from TechNova before Meridian engages any sub-processor to process Customer Data.
> > > > **Escrow**

> > > > We have a preference for Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc. as the escrow agent given our existing relationship and their established protocols. That said, I'm willing to discuss NCC Group if Meridian can demonstrate equivalent capabilities and experience with AI/ML model escrow — I'd appreciate any references or case studies you can share.
> > > > On release triggers, we're aligned: insolvency, material uncured breach exceeding 60 days, and cessation of product support.

> > > > On scope, I want to flag that TechNova's position is that the escrow deposit should include not just the fine-tuned adapter weights but also training configuration and pipeline artifacts necessary to make the escrowed weights independently usable. The weights alone, without the surrounding context, may not be sufficient to enable TechNova to derive value from the escrow in a release scenario.
> > > > **Insurance**

> > > > On Tech E&O: for a TCV exceeding $5,000,000, TechNova's vendor management requirements call for $10,000,000 per occurrence in Tech E&O coverage. The $5,000,000 counter is below our threshold. I'd ask Meridian to make good-faith efforts to secure increased coverage, whether through policy enhancement or an additional excess layer.

> > > > I agree the week of May 19 is appropriate for a joint legal call. On governing law, TechNova's position remains Delaware law, with jurisdiction in the Delaware Court of Chancery or, to the extent subject-matter jurisdiction exists, the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware. We'll address this further in Draft 3. Rachel is working on the markup now, and we're targeting circulation by May 16, 2025.
> > > > Best regards,
> > > > Derek Chalmers
> > > > Vice President & Associate General Counsel
> > > > TechNova Solutions, Inc.
> > > > d.chalmers@technova.com
> > > > > On Wednesday, May 7, 2025, at 9:14 AM EDT, Simone Delacroix <s.delacroix@meridiancognitive.com> wrote:
> > > > > Derek,

> > > > > I hope this finds you well. Following the productive business-side alignment calls between Priya Anand and Jonas Ekberg on May 5–6, Meridian has completed its review of TechNova's Draft 2 counter-markup dated April 21, 2025. Rather than wait for a formal Draft 3 redline, I wanted to capture Meridian's positions on several key legal terms in this email with the goal of narrowing open issues efficiently and identifying areas of agreement before we go back into the document.
> > > > > I've organized this by topic for ease of reference.
> > > > > **1. Intellectual Property: Fine-Tuned Adapter Weights**

> > > > > I've reviewed TechNova's Draft 2 position asserting Customer ownership of all fine-tuned weights and adapter layers (defined as "Customer-Trained Adaptations"). Meridian cannot agree to a full ownership transfer. The Base Model, fine-tuned weights, and derivative models constitute Meridian's intellectual property and are the product of substantial investment in research, development, and training infrastructure.

> > > > > That said, Meridian recognizes TechNova's legitimate interest in continuity and portability. As a compromise, Meridian is prepared to offer TechNova an irrevocable, perpetual, royalty-free license to the fine-tuned adapter weights generated through TechNova's use of MeridianIQ. This license would include extraction and portability rights exercisable upon termination or expiration of the agreement. This represents a meaningful move from our Draft 1 position (dated April 2, 2025), which offered only a limited non-exclusive license that terminated with the agreement.
> > > > > To be clear, Base Model ownership, source code, and proprietary training infrastructure remain exclusively with Meridian in all circumstances.
> > > > > **2. Limitation of Liability**

> > > > > TechNova's Draft 2 proposed a general liability cap of 2× annual fees ($4,800,000, based on an annual platform fee of $2,400,000). Meridian proposes a general liability cap of 1× annual fees ($2,400,000) — a direct dollar-for-dollar cap equal to the annual platform fee. I'll note this is a meaningful upward move from Meridian's Draft 1 position, which was set at 6-month trailing fees ($1,200,000).
> > > > > On carve-outs:
> > > > > - *Willful misconduct and gross negligence:* Meridian accepts uncapped treatment for these categories.

> > > > > - *IP indemnity and data-breach obligations:* Meridian does not agree to treat these as uncapped carve-outs. Instead, we propose a super-cap of 3× annual fees ($7,200,000) for IP indemnity and data-breach-related liability. Notably, this figure equals the full 3-year total contract value, which we believe represents a substantial and commercially reasonable ceiling for these categories.
> > > > > **3. Data Processing & Privacy**

> > > > > Meridian agrees to serve as a "service provider" as defined under the CCPA (Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag)) and to execute a CCPA-compliant Data Processing Addendum. We acknowledge that Customer Data includes consumer nonpublic personal information (NPPI) governed by the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act and the CCPA/CPRA.

> > > > > Meridian does, however, reserve the right to use de-identified and aggregated data derived from Customer Data for model improvement and training purposes. This is standard practice in the AI/ML industry and is essential to maintaining platform quality and the continued advancement of MeridianIQ's capabilities. De-identification will be performed in accordance with applicable law, including the CCPA's de-identification standards.
> > > > > **4. Source Code / Model Escrow**

> > > > > Meridian is willing to establish an escrow arrangement for the fine-tuned adapter weights. To be clear, the escrow would cover fine-tuned adapter weights only — not the full Base Model source code or proprietary training infrastructure.

> > > > > We propose NCC Group plc as the escrow agent, rather than Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc. as specified in TechNova's Draft 2. NCC Group has specific expertise in AI/ML model escrow and verification, which we believe is important given the technical nature of the deposited materials.

> > > > > On release triggers, Meridian's position aligns generally with Draft 2's proposed triggers: insolvency of Meridian, material uncured breach exceeding 60 days, or cessation of product support for MeridianIQ.
> > > > > **5. Insurance**
> > > > > - *Commercial General Liability:* Meridian accepts TechNova's requirement of $5,000,000 per occurrence / $10,000,000 aggregate.
> > > > > - *Umbrella/Excess Liability:* Meridian accepts TechNova's requirement of $10,000,000.

> > > > > - *Technology Errors & Omissions:* Meridian's current policy limit is $5,000,000 per occurrence. We are not in a position to commit to TechNova's $10,000,000 request at this time. We are willing to explore policy enhancement at our next renewal cycle but cannot guarantee increased limits.
> > > > > **6. SLA Terms**
> > > > > The business teams have aligned on 99.95% monthly uptime with standard exclusions for scheduled maintenance and force majeure events, which we consider resolved.

> > > > > On latency, Meridian is willing to move to a commitment of p95 ≤ 450 ms, up from our Draft 1 position of 600 ms. I understand TechNova's Draft 2 requested 400 ms; we believe 450 ms represents a strong and achievable commitment given the complexity of the inference workloads involved.

> > > > > On accuracy, Meridian's position remains F1 ≥ 0.90. We are willing to discuss this further if TechNova can share additional detail on the specific evaluation methodology and dataset composition contemplated for measurement.

> > > > > I'd suggest we schedule a joint legal call during the week of May 19 to work through the remaining open items in real time. I also want to flag that governing law and dispute resolution still need to be addressed — Meridian's position is Massachusetts law with binding AAA arbitration seated in Boston.
> > > > > I look forward to your reactions to the above, Derek. Happy to discuss any of these points by phone in the interim.
> > > > > Best regards,
> > > > > Simone Delacroix
> > > > > Deputy General Counsel
> > > > > Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC
> > > > > s.delacroix@meridiancognitive.com

**\"Agreement\"** means this AI Platform Agreement, including all Exhibits, Schedules, and Statements of Work attached hereto or incorporated by reference herein, as such may be amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time in accordance with the terms hereof.

**\"API\"** means the application programming interfaces, including RESTful APIs and any successor interfaces, through which Customer accesses and interacts with the Platform.

**\"Base Model\"** means Vendor\'s proprietary foundational large language model underlying the Platform, including all neural network architectures, pre-trained weights, and associated algorithms, as such model may be updated, upgraded, or replaced by Vendor from time to time during the Term. **[ARTICLE 2 --- LICENSE GRANT AND SCOPE OF USE]{.underline}**
**Section 2.1 --- License Grant**

Subject to and conditioned upon Customer\'s compliance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement, including timely payment of all Fees, Vendor hereby grants to Customer a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable(except as permitted under Section 14.4), non-sublicensable (except to Affiliates) license during the Term to access and use the Platform solely for Customer\'s internal business operations in connection with Customer\'s lending technology product known as LendStream. The license granted hereunder includes the right to access and use the Platform through the APIs provided by Vendor, to submit Customer Data for processing through the Platform, and to receive and use the outputs generated by the Platform in connection with LendStream. This license is further conditioned on Customer\'s compliance with the Documentation and all applicable laws, rules, and regulations.
**Section 2.2 --- Scope of Authorized Use**

Customer may permit its employees, and authorized contractors who are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth in Article 7, to access and use the Platform on Customer\'s behalf and in furtherance of Customer\'s authorized use hereunder. Customer shall be responsible for all acts and omissions of its employees and authorized contractors in connection with their access to and use of the Platform. Use of the Platform is limited to the processing, analysis, and classification of Customer Data in support of LendStream\'s document processing workflows. Customer shall not use the Platform for any purpose other than as expressly authorized by this Agreement. Customer shall not exceed the Included API Calls in any Contract Year, except as subject to the overage charges set forth in Section 4.3.
**Section 2.3 --- Restrictions**
Customer acknowledges that the Platform and Base Model represent proprietary technology of Vendor. Customer shall not, and shall not permit any third party to:

> \(a\) reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble, or otherwise attempt to derive the source code, algorithms, data structures, or underlying ideas of the Platform or the Base Model, except to the extent that such restriction is expressly prohibited by applicable law notwithstanding a contractual prohibition;

> \(b\) sublicense, sell, resell, lease, rent, loan, distribute, or otherwise make available the Platform or any component thereof to any third party, whether as a service bureau, managed service, or otherwise;

> \(c\) use the Platform or any output thereof for competitive benchmarking, competitive analysis, or to develop, train, or improve a product or service that competes with the Platform or any of Vendor\'s other products or services;
> \(d\) remove, obscure, alter, or deface any proprietary notices, labels, or marks on or in the Platform, the Documentation, or any output thereof;

> \(e\) access the Platform other than through the APIs and access mechanisms provided by Vendor, including without limitation by scraping, crawling, or using any automated means not expressly authorized by Vendor;

> \(f\) attempt to extract, reconstruct, distill, or reverse engineer model weights, architectures, training data, or any other proprietary components from the Platform, whether through prompt injection, model inversion, membership inference, or any other technique; or

> \(g\) use the Platform in any manner that violates applicable law or regulation, or that infringes, misappropriates, or otherwise violates the Intellectual Property Rights or other rights of any third party.
**Section 2.4 --- Reservation of Rights**

Except for the limited license expressly granted in Section 2.1, Vendor reserves all rights in and to the Platformand the Base Model (excluding Customer-Trained Adaptations), including all Intellectual Property Rights therein. No implied licenses are granted under this Agreement by implication, estoppel, or otherwise. Customer\'s right to access and use the Platform is limited to the express license grant set forth in Section 2.1, and all other rights are expressly reserved by Vendor. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to grant Customer any right to access the source code or model weights of the Platform or the Base Model.
**[ARTICLE 3 --- IMPLEMENTATION AND TRAINING SERVICES]{.underline}**
**Section 3.1 --- Implementation Services**

Vendor shall perform the Implementation Services as described in the initial Statement of Work attached hereto as Exhibit A (the \"**Initial SOW**\") and any additional Statements of Work that may be executed by the Parties from time to time pursuant to this Article 3. The Implementation Services under the Initial SOW shall include, without limitation: (a) provisioning and configuration of Customer\'s dedicated Platform environment; (b) API integration of the Platform with Customer\'s LendStream product; (c) fine-tuning of the Base Model using Customer Data to optimize the Platform\'s performance for Customer\'s specific document processing requirements; (d) initial accuracy validation and testing of the fine-tuned model; and (e) initial training of Customer\'s designated personnel on the use and operation of the Platform. All Implementation Services shall be performed by Vendor personnel who are qualified and experienced in the relevant subject matter.
**Section 3.2 --- Implementation Milestones**
The Implementation Services shall be performed in accordance with the following milestones, as further described in Exhibit A:

> **Milestone 1 --- SOW Execution.** Execution of the Initial SOW by both Parties. Achievement of Milestone 1 shall trigger payment of the first installment of the Implementation Fee as set forth in Section 4.2(a).

> **Milestone 2 --- Go-Live.** Successful achievement of Go-Live, targeted for October 1, 2025, at which point the Platform shall be made available for production use by Customer. Achievement of Milestone 2 shall trigger payment of the second installment of the Implementation Fee as set forth in Section 4.2(b). Go-Live shall be conditioned upon the Platform performing materially in accordance with the Documentation, as mutually confirmed by the Parties through the acceptance process described in Exhibit A and Section 3.5.

Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to achieve the targeted Go-Live date, but the targeted Go-Live date is an estimate only and shall not constitute a guaranteed delivery date. Delays caused by Customer\'s failure to fulfill its cooperation obligations under Section 3.3 shall extend the targeted Go-Live date by a commensurate period.
**Section 3.3 --- Customer Cooperation**

Customer acknowledges that Vendor\'s ability to perform the Implementation Services is dependent upon Customer\'s timely cooperation and assistance. Customer shall provide reasonable cooperation in connection with the Implementation Services, including without limitation: (a) timely provision of Customer Data in the format and quality reasonably specified by Vendor; (b) access to Customer\'s systems and environments as reasonably necessary for Vendor to perform API integration and testing; (c) designation of qualified Customer personnel with appropriate subject matter expertise to serve as points of contact and to participate in the implementation process, including providing timely feedback and approvals; and (d) such other cooperation as may be reasonably requested by Vendor and described in the applicable Statement of Work. Customer\'s failure to provide timely cooperation may result in delays in the Implementation Services, and Vendor shall not be responsible for any such delays to the extent caused by Customer\'s failure to perform its cooperation obligations under this Section 3.3.
**Section 3.4 --- Change Orders**

Any changes to the scope, timeline, deliverables, or fees for Implementation Services shall be documented in a mutually agreed written change order signed by authorized representatives of both Parties. No change to the Implementation Services shall be binding unless set forth in a duly executed change order. Each change order shall specify the nature of the change, any impact on the project timeline and milestones, and any additional fees associated with the change. Vendor shall not be obligated to perform any work outside the scope of an executed Statement of Work or change order.
\[ADDED: \### Section 3.5 --- Acceptance Testing

Following completion of implementation and prior to Go-Live, Vendor shall conduct acceptance testing in accordance with mutually agreed test plans and acceptance criteria set forth in the applicable Statement of Work. **[ARTICLE 4 --- FEES AND PAYMENT]{.underline}**
**Section 4.1 --- Annual Platform Fee**

In consideration of the license and access rights granted hereunder, Customer shall pay to Vendor an annual platform fee of Two Million Four Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$2,400,000) per Contract Year (the \"**Annual Platform Fee**\"). The Annual Platform Fee shall be invoiced by Vendor in equal monthly installments of Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$200,000) per month, with each monthly invoice due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice. Vendor shall issue monthly invoices on or about the first business day of each calendar month during the Term, beginning with the first calendar month following the Effective Date.
**Section 4.2 --- Implementation Fee**

In consideration of the Implementation Services described in Article 3 and Exhibit A, Customer shall pay to Vendor a one-time implementation and fine-tuning fee of Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$850,000) (the \"**Implementation Fee**\"). The Implementation Fee shall be payable in two (2) equal installments of Four Hundred Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$425,000) each, as follows:

> \(a\) **First Installment.** Four Hundred Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$425,000), due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice following execution of the Initial SOW (Milestone 1).
> \(b\) **Second Installment.** Four Hundred Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$425,000), due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice following achievement of Go-Live (Milestone 2).
**Section 4.3 --- Overage Fees**

The Annual Platform Fee includes forty million (40,000,000) API calls per Contract Year (the \"**Included API Calls**\"). API calls made by Customer in excess of the Included API Calls during any Contract Year shall be invoiced by Vendor at a rate of twelve-thousandths of a dollar (\$0.012) per API call (the \"**Overage Rate**\"). Overage Fees shall be invoiced monthly in arrears, based on Vendor\'s metering and usage data for the applicable calendar month. Each such invoice shall include a summary of API call usage for the month, including the number of API calls consumed and the number of remaining Included API Calls for the applicable Contract Year. Overage Fee invoices shall be due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice.
**Section 4.4 --- Taxes**

All Fees set forth in this Agreement are exclusive of any and all applicable taxes, duties, levies, or similar governmental charges (collectively, \"**Taxes**\"). Customer shall be responsible for, and shall pay, all sales, use, value-added, goods and services, withholding, and similar Taxes imposed on or in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, excluding taxes based on Vendor\'s net income, capital, or franchise taxes assessed against Vendor. If Vendor is required by law to collect any Taxes from Customer, Vendor shall include such Taxes on the applicable invoice and Customer shall remit payment of such Taxes together with the applicable Fees. If Customer is required to withhold any Taxes from amounts payable to Vendor, Customer shall gross up the payment so that Vendor receives the full amount of the invoiced Fees after deduction of such withholding Taxes.
**Section 4.5 --- Late Payments**

Any undisputed Fees not paid when due shall accrue interest at the lesser of (a) one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month (18% per annum) or (b) the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, from the date such payment was due until the date such payment is received in full by Vendor. In addition, Vendor may, upon at least fifteen (15) days\' prior written notice to Customer, suspend Customer\'s access to the Platform if any undisputed invoice remains unpaid for more than forty-five (45) days past its due date, and such suspension shall continue until all outstanding amounts, including accrued interest, have been paid in full. The foregoing remedies are in addition to, and not in lieu of, any other remedies available to Vendor under this Agreement or applicable law.
**Section 4.6 --- Total Contract Value**
For informational purposes and clarity, the total contract value for the Initial Term (exclusive of Overage Fees and Taxes) is as follows:
> \(a\) Annual Platform Fees for three (3) Contract Years: \$2,400,000 × 3 = **\$7,200,000**;
> \(b\) Implementation Fee (one-time): **\$850,000**;

The foregoing total contract value is an estimate for informational purposes only and does not include any Overage Fees, Taxes, or fees for additional Statements of Work that may be executed during the Term. The total contract value does not limit Vendor\'s right to invoice for Overage Fees or other amounts payable under this Agreement.
\[ADDED: \### Section 4.7 --- Right of Set-Off

Customer shall have the right to set off any amounts owed to Customer under this Agreement (including Service Credits under Article 9 and indemnification obligations under Article 11) against amounts payable by Customer to Vendor.\]
\[ADDED: \### Section 4.8 --- Audit Rights

Vendor shall maintain accurate books and records relating to overage calculations and API call volumes. Customer shall have the right, upon thirty (30) days\' prior written notice, no more than once per Contract Year, to audit or have an independent third-party auditor audit Vendor\'s relevant records to verify the accuracy of invoiced overages. If an audit reveals an overcharge exceeding five percent (5%) of the audited amount, Vendor shall bear the reasonable cost of the audit and promptly refund the overcharge.\]

**[ARTICLE 6 --- DATA PROCESSING AND PRIVACY]{.underline}**
**Section 6.1 --- Customer Data Processing**

Vendor shall process Customer Data solely for the purpose of providing the Platform and performing Vendor\'s obligations under this Agreement. Vendor shall not process Customer Data for any other purpose, including without limitation training, improving, or benchmarking the Base Model or any Derivative Models for the benefit of Vendor or any third party. Vendor shall not sell Customer Data to any third party.
**Section 6.2 --- \[DELETED: Controller\] \[ADDED: Service Provider / Processor\] Status**

Vendor shall process Customer Data solely as a service provider (as defined in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag)) and processor on behalf of Customer. Vendor shall not be deemed an independent controller with respect to any processing of Customer Data. Vendor shall certify its status as a service provider under the CCPA/CPRA in the Data Processing Addendum (Exhibit D).
**Section 6.3 --- Compliance with Laws**

Each Party shall comply with all applicable data protection and privacy laws, rules, and regulations in connection with its processing of Customer Data under this Agreement, including without limitation: (a) the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, 15 U.S.C. §§ 6801--6809, and its implementing regulations, including Regulation S-P (17 C.F.R. Part 248) and the FTC Safeguards Rule (16 C.F.R. Part 314) (\"**GLBA**\"), to the extent applicable to the processing of NPPI; (b) the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018, as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act of 2020, Cal. Civ. Code §§ 1798.100--1798.199.100 (\"**CCPA/CPRA**\"), to the extent applicable; and (c) any other applicable federal, state, or international data protection or privacy laws. Vendor\'s obligations as a service provider under CCPA/CPRA are further set forth in the Data Processing Addendum (Exhibit D).
**Section 6.4 --- Security Measures**

Vendor shall implement and maintain throughout the Term administrative, technical, and physical safeguards that are no less protective than industry-standard measures, including SOC 2 Type II controls, designed to protect Customer Data against unauthorized access, acquisition, use, disclosure, alteration, or destruction. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Vendor\'s security program shall include: (a) encryption of Customer Data in transit (using TLS 1.2 or higher) and at rest (using AES-256 or equivalent); (b) access controls, including multi-factor authentication, role-based access, and least-privilege principles; (c) regular vulnerability assessments and penetration testing; (d) intrusion detection and prevention systems; (e) security incident response procedures; and (f) employee security awareness training. Vendor shall, upon Customer\'s reasonable request and no more than once per twelve (12)-month period, provide Customer with a summary of Vendor\'s then-current security measures and any SOC 2 Type II or equivalent audit reports covering Vendor\'s information security controls.
**Section 6.5 --- Data Breach Notification**

In the event of any confirmed or reasonably suspected security breach involving the unauthorized access, acquisition, use, or disclosure of Customer Data (a \"**Security Breach**\"), Vendor shall: (a) notify Customer of the Security Breach within seventy-two (72) hours of discovery of the Security Breach; (b) promptly investigate the Security Breach and take reasonable steps to contain, mitigate, and remediate the Security Breach; (c) provide Customer with reasonably detailed information regarding the nature and scope of the Security Breach, including the categories and approximate number of data subjects affected, the measures taken or proposed to address the Security Breach, and the identity and contact information of Vendor\'s data protection officer or other contact point; and (d) cooperate with Customer in Customer\'s investigation, response, and notification obligations in connection with the Security Breach. The obligations set forth in this Section 6.5 shall not be construed as an acknowledgment by Vendor of any fault or liability with respect to the Security Breach.

**Section 9.1 --- Uptime**

> **Availability (%) = ((Total Minutes in Month − Downtime Minutes) / Total Minutes in Month) × 100**

For purposes of the Uptime SLA, \"**Downtime**\" means any period during which the Platform is unavailable to Customer for production use, as measured by Vendor\'s monitoring systems. The following events shall be excluded from the calculation of Downtime: (a) scheduled maintenance windows, subject to the limitations and notice requirements set forth in this Section 9.1 and Exhibit B; (b) Force Majeure Events as described in Section 14.5; (c) periods of unavailability caused by Customer\'s systems, networks, or equipment, or by Customer\'s acts or omissions; and (d) periods during which Customer\'s access is suspended by Vendor in accordance with this Agreement (including pursuant to Section 4.5).

Scheduled maintenance windows shall not exceed four (4) hours per calendar month, shall require at least seventy-two (72) hours\' advance written notice to Customer\'s designated technical contact, and shall be scheduled during off-peak hours (between 12:00 AM and 5:00 AM Eastern Time, Saturday or Sunday) to the extent commercially practicable. Maintenance that exceeds four (4) hours in any calendar month, or that is conducted without the requisite seventy-two (72) hours\' advance notice, shall be counted as Downtime for purposes of the Uptime SLA.
**Section 9.2 --- Latency**

Vendor shall maintain API response latency at or below four hundred (400) milliseconds at the ninety-fifth percentile (p95 ≤ 400 ms) during each calendar month, as measured by Vendor\'s internal monitoring systems at the Platform\'s API gateway. Latency shall be measured as the time elapsed between Vendor\'s receipt of an API request at its API gateway and Vendor\'s transmission of the corresponding API response.
**Section 9.3 --- Model Accuracy**

Vendor shall maintain model accuracy, as measured by F1 score, at or above zero point ninety-four (F1 ≥ 0.94), as measured against the mutually agreed validation dataset established during the implementation process, following the conclusion of the Stabilization Period. The validation dataset and F1 score measurement methodology shall be documented in the applicable Statement of Work. The Parties shall review and, if necessary, update the validation dataset no less frequently than once per Contract Year to ensure it remains representative of Customer\'s production document processing workloads.

During the Stabilization Period (ninety (90) days following Go-Live), Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to achieve F1 ≥ 0.90, and shall work collaboratively with Customer to optimize model performance toward the post-stabilization target of F1 ≥ 0.94. Service Credits shall not accrue for model accuracy during the Stabilization Period.

lines.text: **Section 9.2 --- Latency**

Vendor shall maintain API response latency at or below four hundred (400) milliseconds at the ninety-fifth percentile (p95 ≤ 400 ms) during each calendar month, as measured by Vendor\'s internal monitoring systems at the Platform\'s API gateway. Latency shall be measured as the time elapsed between Vendor\'s receipt of an API request at its API gateway and Vendor\'s transmission of the corresponding API response.
**Section 9.3 --- Model Accuracy**

Vendor shall maintain model accuracy, as measured by F1 score, at or above zero point ninety-four (F1 ≥ 0.94), as measured against the mutually agreed validation dataset established during the implementation process, following the conclusion of the Stabilization Period. The validation dataset and F1 score measurement methodology shall be documented in the applicable Statement of Work. The Parties shall review and, if necessary, update the validation dataset no less frequently than once per Contract Year to ensure it remains representative of Customer\'s production document processing workloads.

During the Stabilization Period (ninety (90) days following Go-Live), Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to achieve F1 ≥ 0.90, and shall work collaboratively with Customer to optimize model performance toward the post-stabilization target of F1 ≥ 0.94. Service Credits shall not accrue for model accuracy during the Stabilization Period.
**Section 9.4 --- Service Credits**

In the event Vendor fails to meet the Uptime SLA, API Latency target, or Model Accuracy target in any applicable measurement period, Customer shall be entitled to a service credit in accordance with the service credit schedule set forth in Exhibit B (each, a \"**Service Credit**\"). Service Credits shall be calculated as a percentage of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for the affected calendar month, as set forth in the tiered credit schedule in Exhibit B. If the vendor resists full ownership, move to the irrevocable perpetual license with portability, escrow, and non-assertion conditions set forth in Section 3.2. This concession does not require escalation and should be presented as a commercially reasonable compromise that protects both parties\' interests. Finally, all IP ownership and licensing provisions must be reviewed for consistency with the escrow requirements in Section 7 and the indemnification scope in Section 11. The negotiating attorney should ensure that the escrow deposit scope in the agreement matches the defined scope of \"Customer-Trained Adaptations,\" and that the vendor\'s IP indemnification obligation extends to TechNova\'s authorized use of Customer-Trained Adaptations in addition to the vendor\'s Base Model and platform.

**Service-Provider / Processor Designation.** The vendor must contractually agree to act as a \"service provider\" as defined in California Civil Code Section 1798.140(ag) with respect to all personal information of California residents that the vendor receives, processes, or accesses in connection with the agreement. Where applicable, the vendor must also agree to act as a \"processor\" under the GLBA and its implementing regulations, and to comply with all obligations imposed on processors under those regulations. This designation is mandatory and non-negotiable. A vendor that refuses to accept a service-provider designation, or that insists on being treated as an independent \"business\" or \"controller\" with respect to TechNova customer data, presents a fundamental compliance risk that cannot be mitigated through other contractual mechanisms.

> \(a\) **CCPA Service-Provider Certification.** A certification by the vendor that it understands and will comply with the restrictions applicable to service providers under the CCPA, including the restrictions set forth in California Civil Code Section 1798.140(ag), and that it will not retain, use, or disclose personal information received from TechNova for any purpose other than the specific business purpose set forth in the DPA.

**Prohibition on Third-Party Model Training.** The vendor must be contractually prohibited from using TechNova customer data --- including any derivatives, transformations, embeddings, or representations thereof --- for training, improving, fine-tuning, or otherwise enhancing any models or algorithms for the benefit of third parties or for the benefit of the vendor\'s general-purpose product offerings. This prohibition must extend to all forms of the data, including de-identified or aggregated forms, unless a specific de-identification right has been negotiated in accordance with Section 4.3 below. This prohibition is absolute and non-negotiable.

In certain engagements, a vendor may seek the right to use de-identified or aggregated data derived from TechNova customer data for the purpose of improving the vendor\'s models, algorithms, or platform capabilities. TechNova may consider granting such a right, but only under the following conditions:

**Statutory Standard.** The de-identification must meet the statutory standard set forth in the CCPA at California Civil Code Section 1798.140(m). Specifically, the information must be information that cannot reasonably be used to infer information about, or otherwise be linked to, a particular consumer or household, provided that the vendor (a) has implemented technical safeguards and business processes that prohibit re-identification of the consumer to whom the information may pertain; (b) has implemented business processes to prevent inadvertent release of de-identified information; and (c) makes no attempt to re-identify the information.

**Independent Third-Party Verification.** The de-identification process and its compliance with the statutory standard must be verified by an independent third-party auditor. The auditor must be approved by TechNova in writing prior to the commencement of any audit. The auditor must provide a written certification that the de-identification meets the statutory standard, and this certification must be provided to TechNova before the vendor may make any use of the de-identified data.

**Classification.** Any de-identification right is within the Yellow zone only if both conditions above (statutory standard compliance and independent verification) are satisfied in full. If the vendor proposes a de-identification right without independent third-party verification, or if the proposed de-identification standard does not meet the CCPA statutory standard, the concession falls within the Red zone and requires VP Legal approval before acceptance.

If a vendor proposes a \"controller-to-controller\" or \"independent contractor\" data relationship --- in which the vendor would process TechNova customer data as an independent business or controller with its own rights to use the data --- this is a walk-away absent extraordinary circumstances approved by the General Counsel. A controller-to-controller relationship would expose TechNova to significant regulatory risk under both the GLBA and the CCPA/CPRA, including potential liability for the vendor\'s independent use of customer data, and would undermine TechNova\'s ability to comply with its own privacy obligations to its customers.

Negotiating attorneys should be alert to vendor drafting that attempts to achieve a de facto controller relationship through indirect means, such as broadly defined business purposes, retained rights to \"aggregate\" or \"anonymized\" data without adequate de-identification standards, or carve-outs from the service-provider restrictions for \"product improvement\" or \"model training.\" Any such drafting should be redlined and replaced with the mandatory provisions described in Section 4.2.

The general limitation of liability in any AI/ML vendor agreement sets the maximum aggregate amount that the vendor may be required to pay to TechNova (and vice versa) for all claims arising under the agreement, subject to the carve-outs described in Section 5.2. The following thresholds apply:

**Green (Preferred).** TechNova\'s preferred position is a general liability cap set at two times (2×) the annual fees payable under the agreement. For example, for an agreement with annual fees of \$2,400,000, the preferred general liability cap would be \$4,800,000. This position should be proposed in every initial draft.

**Yellow (Acceptable).** If the vendor will not agree to a 2× annual fees cap, TechNova will accept a general liability cap at one and one-half times (1.5×) the annual fees payable under the agreement. For an agreement with annual fees of \$2,400,000, the acceptable general liability cap would be \$3,600,000. This concession falls within the Yellow zone and may be approved by the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions without further escalation.

**Red (Walk-Away).** Any general liability cap that falls below one times (1×) the annual fees payable under the agreement is a walk-away. For an agreement with annual fees of \$2,400,000, the walk-away floor is \$2,400,000. Acceptance of a general liability cap at or below 1× annual fees requires written approval from the VP Legal, with documented business justification and risk-mitigation measures.

For the avoidance of doubt, the annual fees used to calculate the liability cap should be the annual fees payable in the first year of the agreement (or, for multi-year agreements with escalating fees, the average annual fees over the initial term), unless a different calculation methodology is negotiated. Negotiating attorneys should ensure that the cap is calculated on a consistent basis and that the calculation methodology is clearly stated in the agreement.

Certain categories of liability must be carved out from the general liability cap to ensure that TechNova has adequate recourse in the event of the vendor\'s most serious breaches. The following framework applies:

**Mandatory (Non-Negotiable).** The following categories of liability must remain uncapped --- that is, excluded entirely from the general liability cap --- regardless of the general cap amount negotiated. These carve-outs are mandatory and non-negotiable:
> • **Willful misconduct.** Any liability arising from the vendor\'s willful misconduct.
> • **Gross negligence.** Any liability arising from the vendor\'s gross negligence.

Any vendor attempt to impose a cap on liability for willful misconduct or gross negligence is a Red-zone position and a walk-away. There are no circumstances under which TechNova should accept a cap on these categories.
> • **IP indemnification obligations.** The vendor\'s indemnification obligations with respect to intellectual property infringement claims, as described in Section 11.

**Yellow (Acceptable).** If the vendor will not agree to fully uncapped IP indemnification and data breach obligations, TechNova will accept a \"super-cap\" --- that is, an elevated liability cap for these specific categories --- at a minimum of three times (3×) the annual fees payable under the agreement. For an agreement with annual fees of \$2,400,000, the minimum acceptable super-cap is \$7,200,000. This super-cap applies only to the IP indemnification and data breach carve-outs; the mandatory carve-outs for willful misconduct and gross negligence remain fully uncapped regardless.

> • Any attempt by the vendor to cap liability for willful misconduct or gross negligence, whether through the general cap, a super-cap, or any other mechanism.

Open at 2× annual fees for the general cap and propose fully uncapped treatment for IP indemnity and data breach obligations, in addition to the mandatory uncapped treatment of willful misconduct and gross negligence. This is the Green-tier position and represents TechNova\'s optimal outcome.

If the vendor resists, the following represents an acceptable compromise landing zone: a general cap of 1.5× annual fees, with a super-cap of 3× annual fees for IP indemnity and data breach carve-outs, plus fully uncapped liability for willful misconduct and gross negligence. This combination falls within the Yellow zone and does not require escalation beyond the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions.

All liability positions --- including the general cap, the super-cap (if applicable), and the carve-out structure --- must be documented in the deal approval memorandum for every AI/ML vendor agreement.

**Green (Preferred).** TechNova\'s preferred latency commitment is a p95 response latency of no more than four hundred milliseconds (≤ 400 ms), measured at the vendor\'s API gateway for production inference requests. This threshold is required for real-time, customer-facing applications, including the LendStream product line and any other deployment that involves real-time decisioning, scoring, or response generation in interaction with end users.

A vendor offer in the range of 401--500 ms falls within the acceptable zone but below the preferred threshold. Negotiating attorneys should make a good-faith effort to secure a commitment at or below 400 ms before accepting a latency commitment in the 401--500 ms range.

If the vendor\'s best offer falls within the 401--500 ms range (e.g., 450 ms p95), the negotiating attorney should flag the offer to Product Engineering for confirmation that the specific use case can tolerate the additional latency. For example, a 450 ms commitment may be acceptable for batch processing or non-time-critical analytics, but may not be acceptable for LendStream real-time decisioning, where even 50 ms of additional latency can materially affect conversion rates and customer experience. This threshold applies to any deployment that directly serves or interacts with TechNova\'s customers in real time. For internal-only, non-customer-facing deployments (e.g., internal analytics, back-office model inference), the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions may approve a latency commitment above 500 ms on a case-by-case basis, subject to Product Engineering\'s written confirmation that the higher latency does not impact customer experience.

**Green (Preferred).** TechNova\'s preferred model accuracy commitment is an F1 score of at least 0.95 on agreed benchmark datasets. The benchmark datasets must be mutually agreed upon at the time of contract execution and must be representative of TechNova\'s production data distribution. The F1 score should be calculated on the basis of the agreed evaluation methodology, including the specific precision and recall definitions applicable to TechNova\'s use case.

**Yellow (Acceptable).** TechNova will accept a model accuracy commitment with an F1 score of at least 0.92 on agreed benchmark datasets. An F1 score of 0.92 is the Playbook minimum; no accuracy commitment below this threshold is acceptable without escalation.

**Red (Walk-Away).** Any accuracy commitment below an F1 score of 0.92 is a walk-away. A vendor that cannot commit to at least F1 ≥ 0.92 on agreed benchmark datasets is not able to meet TechNova\'s minimum performance requirements.

Every AI/ML vendor agreement must include a termination right that may be exercised by TechNova in the event of chronic SLA underperformance. Chronic underperformance is defined as a material SLA miss --- including uptime, latency, or accuracy failures --- in three (3) or more consecutive calendar months.

For latency, the negotiating attorney should push firmly for a commitment at or below 400 ms p95, especially for any deployment supporting the LendStream platform or other real-time consumer-facing products. If the vendor counters with a latency commitment between 400 ms and 500 ms, the negotiating attorney should coordinate with the VP of Product Engineering (currently Priya Anand) before accepting. Product Engineering\'s assessment of whether the specific use case can tolerate the proposed latency should be documented in the negotiation file.

For accuracy, an F1 score of 0.92 is the absolute minimum; the preferred threshold is 0.95. A stabilization ramp period is acceptable only if the post-stabilization target meets or exceeds the preferred threshold, and only if the agreement provides TechNova with a termination right if the target is not achieved by the end of the ramp period.

There is no exception to this requirement. If the TCV exceeds \$1,000,000, the escrow provision must be included in the agreement itself (as a section or exhibit) or in a standalone three-party escrow agreement executed concurrently with the vendor agreement. An AI/ML vendor agreement with a TCV exceeding \$1,000,000 that does not include an escrow provision --- or that is not accompanied by a concurrently executed standalone escrow agreement --- may not be approved for execution.

Deposits must be updated no less frequently than quarterly (i.e., at least once every ninety (90) calendar days), or upon any material model version update (e.g., retraining, architecture change, or significant hyperparameter adjustment), whichever is more frequent. Each deposit update must be accompanied by a verification report from the escrow agent confirming receipt and completeness of the deposit materials.

The notice must identify the breach with reasonable specificity and state TechNova\'s intent to invoke the escrow release upon expiration of the cure period.

Release must be automatic upon verification of the trigger event by the escrow agent. The escrow agent must be authorized under the escrow agreement to verify the occurrence of the trigger event based on documentation provided by TechNova (e.g., copies of bankruptcy filings, written breach notices, vendor end-of-life announcements) and to release the escrow materials to TechNova without requiring the vendor\'s consent, approval, or cooperation.

If the vendor insists on an alternative escrow agent, accept only a Tier 1 provider with verifiable AI/ML escrow capabilities. Do not accept a general-purpose escrow agent that lacks specific experience with AI/ML model artifacts, as such agents may not have the technical infrastructure or processes necessary to handle large model files, verify deposit completeness, or support the quarterly update cadence required by this Playbook.

Every AI/ML vendor must maintain commercial general liability insurance with minimum limits of five million dollars (\$5,000,000) per occurrence and ten million dollars (\$10,000,000) in the aggregate. **8.2 --- Technology Errors & Omissions (Tech E&O)**

**Red (Walk-Away).** Any Tech E&O coverage below \$5,000,000 per occurrence is a walk-away. Acceptance of a Tech E&O limit below \$5,000,000 requires VP Legal approval with a documented risk assessment.
