If the vendor\'s current policy limit is \$5,000,000, explore whether the vendor is willing to obtain an endorsement, policy amendment, or increased limits as a condition of the agreement. The cost of increased coverage should be borne by the vendor and should not be passed through to TechNova. If the vendor demonstrates that \$10,000,000 in Tech E&O coverage is not commercially available or is prohibitively expensive, the negotiating attorney should escalate to the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions with a written risk assessment before accepting the \$5,000,000 minimum.

Every AI/ML vendor must maintain umbrella or excess liability insurance with a minimum limit of ten million dollars (\$10,000,000). This coverage must sit excess of the vendor\'s CGL and Tech E&O policies and must provide coverage for claims that exceed the underlying policy limits.

TechNova\'s preferred position is that the vendor provides a full indemnity to TechNova for third-party claims related to AI-generated outputs. Specifically, the vendor\'s indemnity must cover:

The vendor may not condition the indemnity on TechNova\'s use of the outputs in a specific manner beyond what is set forth in the agreement and the vendor\'s documentation.

> \(b\) **Unauthorized Use.** Claims arising from TechNova\'s use of outputs outside the documented use case or in a manner inconsistent with the vendor\'s published usage guidelines. For example, if the vendor\'s usage guidelines expressly prohibit the use of a particular model for credit decisioning, and TechNova uses the model for credit decisioning notwithstanding that prohibition, the vendor\'s indemnity obligation does not apply to claims arising from that unauthorized use.

AI-output risk allocation is a relatively novel provision in AI/ML vendor agreements, and many vendors will not have standard language addressing this issue. Negotiating attorneys should be prepared to propose TechNova\'s preferred position (Section 9.2) in the initial draft and to educate vendor counsel on the rationale for the provision. The key points to communicate are:

If the vendor has not previously addressed AI-output risk allocation in its standard terms, the shared-risk framework described in Section 9.3 is an acceptable landing zone and should be presented as a reasonable compromise. Emphasize that the shared-risk framework limits the vendor\'s exposure to the applicable liability cap or super-cap, which already constrains the vendor\'s total financial exposure.

Negotiating attorneys should coordinate with Product Engineering to document the specific use cases and output types that will be covered by the AI-output indemnity. A clear and specific description of \"authorized use\" will strengthen TechNova\'s position in any future claim and will provide the vendor with reasonable certainty about the scope of its obligation.

Any vendor that categorically refuses both the full indemnity (Section 9.2) and the shared-risk framework (Section 9.3) --- that is, any vendor that takes the position that it has no responsibility whatsoever for claims arising from its model\'s outputs --- should be flagged for escalation to the VP Legal. **Green (Preferred) / Minimum (Non-Negotiable).** The vendor\'s intellectual property indemnity must cover all forms of intellectual property rights, without limitation. Specifically, the indemnity must cover claims alleging infringement, misappropriation, or violation of:

The indemnity must not be limited to registered United States patents and copyrights. Many vendor form agreements contain IP indemnity provisions that are narrowly scoped to cover only \"infringement of a valid, issued U.S. patent or registered U.S. copyright.\" This narrow scope is insufficient for TechNova\'s purposes, as it would leave TechNova without indemnification coverage for trade secret misappropriation claims (which are increasingly common in the AI/ML space), trademark infringement claims, foreign IP claims, and claims based on unregistered copyrights. Line 11: Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc. (\"Iron Mountain IPM\" or \"Escrow Agent\") provides a standard three-party technology escrow service designed to safeguard the interests of licensees and customers of proprietary technology. By requiring the vendor (the \"Depositor\") to place current and complete copies of the technology in escrow, the arrangement provides meaningful assurance to the licensee (the \"Beneficiary\") that it will retain the ability to access, maintain, and, where applicable, reconstruct the deposited technology in the event the Depositor is unable or unwilling to continue providing support, maintenance, or access to the technology.

(\"Iron Mountain IPM\" or \"Escrow Agent\") provides a standard three-party technology escrow service designed to safeguard the interests of licensees and customers of proprietary technology. The escrow arrangement ensures that critical technology assets --- including, without limitation, source code, machine-learning model weights, training data configurations, and related technical documentation --- are deposited with a neutral, independent escrow agent and held securely for the benefit of a designated beneficiary. In the event that specified release conditions occur, the deposited materials are made available to the beneficiary so that the beneficiary may continue to use, maintain, and operate the technology in accordance with the rights granted under the underlying license or vendor agreement.

The Iron Mountain IPM technology escrow service is widely recognized as an industry-standard mechanism for mitigating the risks associated with dependence on a single technology vendor. By requiring the vendor (the \"Depositor\") to place current and complete copies of the technology in escrow, the arrangement provides meaningful assurance to the licensee (the \"Beneficiary\") that it will retain the ability to access, maintain, and, where applicable, reconstruct the deposited technology in the event the Depositor is unable or unwilling to continue providing support, maintenance, or access to the technology.

**This summary is provided for reference and informational purposes only.** It is intended to facilitate internal review and evaluation by TechNova Solutions, Inc. (\"TechNova\" or \"Beneficiary\") in connection with the proposed escrow arrangement involving Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC (\"Meridian\" or \"Depositor\"). The governing terms of the escrow arrangement will be set forth exclusively in a fully executed Technology Escrow Agreement (the \"Escrow Agreement\") among the three parties --- Iron Mountain IPM, Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC, and TechNova Solutions, Inc. In the event of any conflict or inconsistency between this summary and the executed Escrow Agreement, the terms of the executed Escrow Agreement shall control in all respects.

Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC is the owner and licensor of the proprietary cognitive analytics platform and associated machine-learning models licensed to TechNova Solutions, Inc. under the parties\' underlying Master Software License and Services Agreement. Meridian will be responsible for depositing and maintaining all specified technology assets in escrow in accordance with the terms of the Escrow Agreement.

**Beneficiary (Customer):** The licensee or customer entitled to receive copies of the deposited materials upon the occurrence of a qualifying release event. The Beneficiary has the right to request release of the deposit materials, to request verification of the completeness and accuracy of the deposit, and to receive notice of certain events relating to the escrow arrangement. For purposes of this summary, the anticipated Beneficiary is:

**Escrow Agent:** The independent, neutral third party responsible for receiving, securely storing, and, upon the occurrence of specified release conditions or as otherwise directed, releasing the deposited materials. The Escrow Agent has no ownership interest in the deposited materials and acts solely in a custodial and administrative capacity. The Escrow Agent for this arrangement is:
> **Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc.** A subsidiary of Iron Mountain Incorporated

Iron Mountain IPM maintains secure, geographically redundant storage facilities and employs industry-standard security protocols to protect the confidentiality and integrity of all deposited materials throughout the term of the escrow arrangement. Iron Mountain IPM\'s obligations are limited to those expressly set forth in the Escrow Agreement, and Iron Mountain IPM does not assume any obligations under the underlying license or vendor agreement between the Depositor and the Beneficiary.

> • All build scripts, makefiles, configuration files, and continuous-integration/continuous-deployment (CI/CD) pipeline definitions necessary to compile, link, and package the deposited technology into deployable form;
**B. Model Weights.** All machine-learning model weights associated with the deposited technology, including:
> • Base model weights for all foundational models used by the deposited technology;

> • Fine-tuned adapter weights (e.g., LoRA, QLoRA, or similar parameter-efficient fine-tuning artifacts) and any associated configuration files specifying adapter architecture, rank, and merging instructions;
> • Model checkpoint files for each production-release version of the deposited technology;

The specific model weights to be deposited shall be identified by mutual agreement of Depositor and Beneficiary and set forth in the deposit description schedule. Where the deposited technology incorporates third-party base models subject to separate license terms, the Depositor shall identify those models and provide copies of the applicable license terms to the extent necessary for the Beneficiary to understand the scope of rights available upon release.

**C. Training Data Configurations and Pipeline Artifacts.** All configurations, scripts, and artifacts necessary to understand and, where feasible, reproduce the training pipeline for the deposited models, including:
> • Hyperparameter specifications for each training run associated with a production-release model;
> • Data preprocessing scripts, data cleaning pipelines, and feature-engineering code;
> • Data pipeline orchestration scripts and workflow definitions;

For the avoidance of doubt, the deposit of training data configurations and pipeline artifacts does not necessarily require the deposit of the underlying raw training data itself. The inclusion or exclusion of raw training data shall be determined by mutual agreement of Depositor and Beneficiary, taking into account data licensing restrictions, data volume, and the practical requirements for maintaining and retraining the deposited models. Where raw training data is not included, Depositor shall provide sufficient documentation to identify all training data sources, describe any licensing or access requirements, and enable the Beneficiary to obtain the necessary data independently.

**Format Requirements.** All deposit materials shall be delivered in industry-standard, machine-readable formats agreed upon by the parties. Source code and scripts shall be delivered in their native file formats (e.g., .py, .java, .js, .go, .rs, .cpp, .h, .yaml, .json, .toml). Model weights shall be delivered in widely supported serialization formats (e.g., PyTorch .pt/.pth, TensorFlow SavedModel, ONNX, SafeTensors). Documentation shall be delivered in portable formats (e.g., PDF, Markdown, HTML). The Depositor shall include a top-level README file providing an index and description of all deposited materials.

Timely and regular deposits are essential to ensure that the escrowed materials remain current and useful in the event of a release. The Escrow Agreement will establish the following deposit and update obligations:

**A. Initial Deposit.** The Depositor shall deliver a complete initial deposit of all deposit materials described in Section III above to the Escrow Agent within thirty (30) calendar days following the date of full execution of the Escrow Agreement by all three parties. The initial deposit shall include all materials corresponding to the then-current production release version of the deposited technology as of the date of the Escrow Agreement.

The Depositor shall accompany each deposit (including the initial deposit) with a completed deposit description form, in the format prescribed by Iron Mountain IPM, identifying the materials included in the deposit, the version or release number of the deposited technology, the date of the deposit, and a manifest listing all files and directories included in the deposit together with file sizes and checksums (e.g., SHA-256 hashes) sufficient to verify file integrity.

> • Within fifteen (15) business days following each major release, minor release, or material update to the deposited technology that is made available to the Beneficiary under the underlying agreement,

whichever results in more frequent updates. For purposes of this requirement, a \"material update\" includes any update that introduces new functionality, modifies the model architecture, retrains or fine-tunes model weights, changes the build or deployment process in a manner that would affect the Beneficiary\'s ability to build or deploy the technology, or addresses a critical security vulnerability.

**C. Deposit Media and Delivery Method.** All deposits shall be delivered via secure electronic transfer to Iron Mountain IPM\'s designated secure repository. Iron Mountain IPM will provide the Depositor with access credentials and transfer instructions upon execution of the Escrow Agreement. Electronic transfers shall be encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher and shall be encrypted at rest within Iron Mountain IPM\'s storage infrastructure.

Physical media deposits (e.g., encrypted USB drives, encrypted hard drives) will be accepted upon request, provided that the Depositor coordinates delivery logistics with Iron Mountain IPM in advance and that all physical media are encrypted using AES-256 or equivalent encryption, with decryption keys delivered separately to Iron Mountain IPM via a secure, out-of-band channel.

Iron Mountain IPM offers optional technical verification services designed to confirm that the deposited materials are complete, readable, and, at the highest verification tier, operationally functional. Verification provides an important layer of assurance to the Beneficiary that the deposited materials will be useful and usable in the event of a release.
Iron Mountain IPM\'s verification services are available at three tiers, described below in order of increasing depth and rigor:

Upon completion of Level 1 verification, Iron Mountain IPM will provide a written verification report to both Depositor and Beneficiary identifying any discrepancies and confirming whether the deposit contents match the manifest. Level 1 verification does not include any assessment of file readability, format correctness, content completeness, or technical functionality.

Upon completion of Level 2 verification, Iron Mountain IPM will provide a detailed written verification report identifying the results of each verification step, including any identified gaps, deficiencies, or areas of concern. Level 2 verification does not include any attempt to compile, build, or execute the deposited technology.

**Iron Mountain IPM recommends Level 2 verification at minimum for deposits involving machine-learning model weights and training configurations.** Deposits of this nature are inherently complex and may involve large binary files, specialized serialization formats, and interdependencies among model components, training artifacts, and deployment infrastructure. Level 2 verification helps to ensure that the deposited materials are readable and organized in a manner that would be useful to the Beneficiary in the event of a release, and that critical components such as model weight files, adapter configurations, and training pipeline scripts are present and accounted for.
> • Attempt to load and instantiate deposited model weights using the deposited configuration files and code;

Level 3 verification is performed by Iron Mountain IPM\'s technical verification team, which includes engineers with experience in software development, DevOps, and machine-learning engineering. The scope, timeline, and cost of Level 3 verification are determined on a case-by-case basis depending on the complexity of the deposited technology and the requirements of the build or deployment process. Iron Mountain IPM will provide a detailed scope-of-work estimate prior to commencing Level 3 verification.

Upon completion of Level 3 verification, Iron Mountain IPM will provide a comprehensive written verification report documenting the verification methodology, the environment specifications, the results of each verification step, and any identified deficiencies or recommendations for improving the deposit.

The central purpose of the escrow arrangement is to ensure that the Beneficiary has access to the deposited technology assets in the event that specified release conditions occur. The Escrow Agent shall release a complete copy of the then-current deposit materials to the Beneficiary upon written certification by the Beneficiary, and subject to the dispute-resolution process described in Section VII below, that one or more of the following release conditions has occurred:

**1. Insolvency Event.** The Depositor files a voluntary petition for relief under any chapter of the United States Bankruptcy Code (Title 11, United States Code) or any analogous insolvency law of any jurisdiction; or an involuntary petition is filed against the Depositor under any such law and is not dismissed within sixty (60) days of filing; or the Depositor is the subject of proceedings for receivership, liquidation, dissolution, or winding up; or the Depositor makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors; or the Depositor admits in writing its inability to pay its debts as they become due.

An insolvency event represents a fundamental threat to the Beneficiary\'s continued access to the deposited technology, as the Depositor\'s ability to provide ongoing support, maintenance, and development may be severely compromised or eliminated entirely. Release upon an insolvency event is intended to protect the Beneficiary\'s investment in the licensed technology and to ensure operational continuity.

**2. Material Uncured Breach.** The Depositor commits a material breach of the underlying Master Software License and Services Agreement or other vendor agreement between the Depositor and the Beneficiary, and such breach remains uncured for a period of sixty (60) calendar days following written notice from the Beneficiary to the Depositor specifying the nature of the breach in reasonable detail. If the underlying agreement between the Depositor and the Beneficiary specifies a different cure period for material breaches, the cure period specified in the underlying agreement shall govern for purposes of this release condition.

**3. Cessation of Product Support.** The Depositor ceases to maintain or support the deposited technology, including by failing to provide updates, patches, bug fixes, or technical support in accordance with the terms of the underlying agreement; or the Depositor publicly announces the discontinuation, end-of-life, or sunsetting of the product line that includes the deposited technology; and in either case, the Depositor fails to provide a reasonable transition plan to the Beneficiary within sixty (60) calendar days following the Beneficiary\'s written request for such a plan. A \"reasonable transition plan\" shall, at minimum, include a timeline for transition, a description of the steps the Depositor will take to facilitate the Beneficiary\'s migration to an alternative solution or assumption of self-maintenance responsibilities, and cooperation with the Beneficiary\'s technical team during the transition period.

**4. Additional Triggers.** Any other release conditions mutually agreed upon in writing by the Depositor and the Beneficiary and expressly set forth in the Escrow Agreement or in a written amendment thereto executed by all three parties. The parties may, by way of example and not limitation, agree to include release conditions triggered by a change of control of the Depositor, the Depositor\'s failure to meet specified service-level commitments over a defined measurement period, or the Depositor\'s failure to deliver updated deposits within the timeframes specified in the Escrow Agreement.

**Scope of Release.** Upon the occurrence of a qualifying release event and the completion of the notice and dispute-resolution procedures set forth in Section VII below, the Escrow Agent shall deliver to the Beneficiary a complete copy of the then-current deposit materials held in escrow. The release of deposit materials to the Beneficiary does not transfer any ownership rights in the deposited materials; the Beneficiary\'s rights to use the released materials shall be governed by and limited to the terms of the underlying agreement between the Depositor and the Beneficiary, any applicable intellectual property licenses, and the terms of the Escrow Agreement.

The Escrow Agreement will include a structured dispute-resolution process to protect the interests of both the Depositor and the Beneficiary in the event that a release request is contested. The standard dispute-resolution process operates as follows:

**A. Notice to Depositor.** Upon receipt of a written release request from the Beneficiary (together with the Beneficiary\'s written certification that one or more release conditions has occurred), the Escrow Agent shall provide written notice to the Depositor within five (5) business days of receipt of the release request. The notice shall include a copy of the Beneficiary\'s release request and certification and shall inform the Depositor of its right to object to the release within the timeframe specified below.

**C. Effect of Objection.** If the Depositor timely delivers a written objection within the thirty (30) calendar day period, the deposit materials shall remain in escrow and shall not be released to the Beneficiary pending resolution of the dispute. The dispute may be resolved by any of the following means:

> \(a\) **Mutual Written Agreement.** The Depositor and the Beneficiary may resolve the dispute by mutual written agreement, which may include an agreement to release, an agreement not to release, or an agreement to release subject to specified conditions or limitations. Upon receipt of a mutual written agreement signed by both the Depositor and the Beneficiary directing the Escrow Agent to release or withhold the deposit materials, the Escrow Agent shall act in accordance with the instructions set forth in such agreement.

> \(b\) **Binding Arbitration.** Either the Depositor or the Beneficiary may initiate binding arbitration in accordance with the arbitration provisions set forth in the Escrow Agreement. Unless otherwise specified in the Escrow Agreement, arbitration shall be conducted under the Commercial Arbitration Rules of the American Arbitration Association by a single arbitrator with relevant technology industry experience, and the arbitration shall take place in Boston, Massachusetts, or such other location as the parties may agree. The Escrow Agent shall comply with any final, binding arbitration award directing the release or withholding of deposit materials.

> \(c\) **Final Court Order.** Either the Depositor or the Beneficiary may seek a final, non-appealable order from a court of competent jurisdiction directing the release or withholding of deposit materials. The Escrow Agent shall comply with any such order upon receipt of a certified copy thereof.

**D. Failure to Object.** If the Depositor does not deliver a written objection to the Escrow Agent within the thirty (30) calendar day period following receipt of the Escrow Agent\'s notice, the Escrow Agent shall release a complete copy of the then-current deposit materials to the Beneficiary as promptly as practicable, and in no event later than fifteen (15) business days following the expiration of the objection period.

**E. Escrow Agent\'s Role.** The Escrow Agent\'s role in the dispute-resolution process is strictly administrative. The Escrow Agent is not required to evaluate the merits of the Beneficiary\'s release request or the Depositor\'s objection, to determine whether a release condition has in fact occurred, or to mediate or adjudicate any dispute between the Depositor and the Beneficiary. The Escrow Agent shall be entitled to rely conclusively on the written certifications, objections, agreements, arbitration awards, and court orders received from the parties without independent investigation.

The following fee schedule reflects Iron Mountain IPM\'s standard pricing for technology escrow services. Fees are quoted on an annual basis and are payable in advance upon execution of the Escrow Agreement and on each anniversary thereof throughout the term.
Base escrow administration (single beneficiary)   \$2,500 -- \$5,000

> • The base escrow administration fee covers the receipt, secure storage, and administrative management of deposit materials for one Depositor and one Beneficiary, including processing of up to four (4) routine deposit updates per year.

> • Additional beneficiary fees apply for each beneficiary beyond the first that is added to the escrow arrangement. Each additional beneficiary is entitled to the same release rights and notice procedures as the initial Beneficiary.

> • Level 2 and Level 3 verification fees vary based on the size and complexity of the deposit, the number and type of technologies involved, and the scope of the verification engagement. Iron Mountain IPM will provide a fee estimate prior to commencing any Level 2 or Level 3 verification engagement.

> • Level 3 verification fees for complex deposits involving large-scale machine-learning models, multi-component software systems, or specialized hardware dependencies may exceed the standard range. Iron Mountain IPM will provide a detailed scope-of-work and fee proposal for any Level 3 engagement anticipated to exceed \$25,000.

All fees are subject to the then-current Iron Mountain IPM fee schedule in effect at the time of execution of the Escrow Agreement. Custom pricing is available for high-value or complex deposits, multi-agreement programs, and enterprise-scale escrow arrangements. Iron Mountain IPM will provide a formal fee proposal upon request.

Iron Mountain IPM\'s role under the Escrow Agreement is limited to that of an independent custodian and administrative agent. The Escrow Agreement will include the following limitation-of-liability provisions with respect to the Escrow Agent:

**Aggregate Liability Cap.** Iron Mountain IPM\'s total aggregate liability to the Depositor, the Beneficiary, and any other party arising out of or related to the Escrow Agreement, whether based in contract, tort, negligence, strict liability, or any other legal or equitable theory, shall not exceed the total fees actually paid to Iron Mountain IPM under the Escrow Agreement during the twelve (12) month period immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim.

**Exclusion of Consequential Damages.** In no event shall Iron Mountain IPM be liable for any indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive, or exemplary damages, including without limitation damages for lost profits, lost revenue, lost data, business interruption, or loss of business opportunity, arising out of or related to the Escrow Agreement, regardless of whether such damages were foreseeable or whether Iron Mountain IPM was advised of the possibility of such damages.

**No Responsibility for Deposit Materials.** Iron Mountain IPM assumes no responsibility whatsoever for the completeness, accuracy, quality, functionality, fitness for a particular purpose, or merchantability of the deposited materials. Iron Mountain IPM does not represent or warrant that the deposited materials are sufficient to build, deploy, operate, or maintain the deposited technology, or that the deposited materials are free from defects, errors, viruses, or malicious code. Iron Mountain IPM\'s sole obligation with respect to the deposited materials is to securely store the materials as received from the Depositor and to release the materials in accordance with the terms of the Escrow Agreement.

**Reliance on Instructions.** Iron Mountain IPM shall be entitled to act in reliance upon any written instruction, certification, notice, objection, agreement, arbitration award, or court order that it reasonably believes to be genuine and to have been signed or delivered by an authorized representative of the applicable party. Iron Mountain IPM shall have no liability for any action taken or omitted in good faith reliance upon such instructions.

The limitation-of-liability provisions set forth in this section are material to Iron Mountain IPM\'s willingness to serve as Escrow Agent and are reflected in the fee structure for the escrow services. The parties acknowledge that the fees charged by Iron Mountain IPM are set in consideration of these limitations and would be substantially higher in the absence of such limitations.

For additional information regarding Iron Mountain IPM technology escrow services, to request a formal fee proposal, or to initiate the process of establishing a technology escrow arrangement, please contact:
> **Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc.** Account Services --- Technology Escrow
> Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc. One Federal Street Boston, MA 02110

Iron Mountain IPM account representatives are available to discuss escrow structure, verification requirements, fee proposals, and customization of escrow terms to meet the specific needs of the Depositor and Beneficiary.

**NOTICE:** This summary is provided for informational and reference purposes only in connection with TechNova Solutions, Inc. internal reference no. TNS-VENDOR-2025-0043 and does not constitute a binding agreement, offer, or commitment by Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc., Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC, or TechNova Solutions, Inc. Binding terms shall be governed exclusively by the executed Technology Escrow Agreement among the parties. This summary is confidential and intended solely for the internal use of TechNova Solutions, Inc. and its authorized advisors in evaluating the proposed escrow arrangement. Distribution of this summary to third parties without the prior written consent of Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc. is prohibited.

Line 19: MeridianIQ addresses a critical operational bottleneck in the mortgage lifecycle: the manual review, indexing, and data entry associated with the high volume and wide variety of documents generated during loan origination, underwriting, and closing. By automating these processes at the model level, MeridianIQ enables customers to reduce processing time, improve data accuracy, and free human reviewers to focus on exception handling and quality assurance rather than routine data extraction tasks.
Line 21: The platform\'s target customer profile includes mortgage lenders, loan servicers, fintech platforms, and banks requiring high-throughput document intelligence at scale. MeridianIQ is designed to integrate seamlessly into existing loan origination systems (LOS), point-of-sale platforms, and servicing technologies via a well-documented RESTful API, enabling customers to embed intelligent document processing directly into their production workflows without disrupting existing system architectures.
Line 37: Additional document classes beyond the standard set listed above are available through customer-specific fine-tuning engagements. During the implementation phase, Meridian works with the customer to identify additional document types relevant to the customer\'s workflows and trains custom adapter layers to support extraction from those formats. Common examples of customer-specific document classes include bank statements, asset verification letters, flood certifications, homeowners insurance declarations pages, and investor-specific stacking order checklists.
Line 51: **Structured JSON Output for Downstream Integration.** All extraction results, classification labels, confidence scores, reconciliation findings, and compliance flags are returned in a structured JSON format designed for direct consumption by downstream systems such as loan origination systems, data warehouses, underwriting engines, and quality control platforms. The JSON schema is fully documented and versioned, and Meridian provides schema migration guidance when breaking changes are introduced in new API versions.
Line 61: **Fine-Tuning Framework.** MeridianIQ employs a modular adapter layer architecture based on Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) principles. This approach enables customer-specific customization without modifying the underlying base model weights. During the implementation engagement, Meridian trains adapter layers on customer-provided labeled document sets to adapt the model\'s extraction behavior to the customer\'s specific document formats, terminology, field naming conventions, and extraction schemas. Because the base model weights remain frozen during adapter training, this approach is computationally efficient, preserves the base model\'s generalized document understanding capabilities, and ensures that customer-specific customizations do not interfere with other tenants\' adapter configurations.
Line 63: **Adapter Layer Architecture.** Each customer\'s adapter weights are stored independently and applied dynamically at inference time. When a document is submitted for processing, the inference pipeline identifies the appropriate tenant and loads the corresponding adapter weights atop the frozen base model. This design allows Meridian to maintain a single base model version across all tenants while delivering customer-specific extraction performance. Adapter weights are versioned, and customers can maintain multiple adapter versions (e.g., for A/B testing or staged rollouts) simultaneously.
Line 67: 1\. **Document Ingestion:** The submitted document file is received via the API, validated for format and size compliance, and queued for processing.
Line 73: 4\. **Extraction via Base Model + Adapter:** The classified document is processed by the base model with the tenant\'s applicable adapter weights loaded, producing raw extraction outputs for each target field in the document class schema.
Line 77: 6\. **Structured Output:** The final extraction results, classification label, confidence scores, reconciliation findings, and compliance flags are assembled into the structured JSON response payload and returned to the customer via the API or webhook callback.
Line 83: **2.2.1 Multi-Tenant SaaS (Standard).** The standard deployment option hosts the customer\'s workloads on shared compute infrastructure with logical tenant isolation enforced at every layer of the stack. Data segregation is maintained at the application layer (tenant-scoped API authentication and authorization), the storage layer (tenant-partitioned database schemas and isolated object storage buckets), and the network layer (security group and network policy enforcement). Each tenant\'s adapter weights are stored in isolated, encrypted object storage containers that are accessible only by the inference pipeline processes operating on behalf of that specific tenant.
Line 89: The dedicated instance option is available at additional cost; pricing is determined based on the customer\'s throughput requirements, compute resource allocation, storage volume, and support tier, and is provided upon request. Dedicated instances also support enhanced security configurations including customer-managed encryption keys (CMK), mutual TLS (mTLS) for API authentication, and private network connectivity via AWS PrivateLink.
Line 99: **Primary Region:** US East (N. Virginia) --- \`us-east-1\`. The primary region hosts all production workloads under normal operating conditions, including the API gateway, inference fleet, database tier, object storage, and supporting microservices.
Line 113: **Auto-Scaling Inference Fleet.** The GPU-accelerated inference fleet is configured with auto-scaling policies that dynamically adjust compute capacity based on real-time demand signals including request queue depth, GPU utilization, and latency metrics. A minimum baseline capacity is reserved per tenant to ensure consistent performance during traffic spikes and to prevent resource contention between tenants on the multi-tenant deployment.
Line 115: **Load Balancing.** Incoming API traffic is distributed across the inference fleet via AWS Application Load Balancer (ALB) with health-check-based routing. The ALB continuously monitors the health of backend inference instances and automatically removes unhealthy instances from the target group, redistributing traffic to healthy instances without interruption to the customer.
Line 123: **Continuous Replication.** All tenant data---including processed documents, extraction results, configuration data, and adapter weights---is continuously replicated from the primary region (\`us-east-1\`) to the failover region (\`us-west-2\`). Replication is performed at both the database level (Aurora cross-region replication) and the object storage level (S3 cross-region replication), ensuring that the failover region maintains a near-real-time copy of all critical data.
Line 127: **Backup Retention.** Database snapshots are retained on a 30-day rolling basis, providing point-in-time recovery capability for the most recent 30-day window. Object storage items---including adapter weights, pipeline artifacts, and processed document outputs---are retained for 90 days in both the primary and failover regions. Backup encryption is consistent with the platform\'s data-at-rest encryption standards described in Section 6.1.
Line 129: **[4. API Specifications]{.underline}**
Line 131: **4.1 General.** MeridianIQ exposes a RESTful HTTPS API as the primary interface for all document submission, processing, extraction retrieval, and platform management operations. The API is designed to be intuitive for developers familiar with modern REST conventions and follows consistent patterns across all endpoints.
Line 133: > • **Protocol:** RESTful API served exclusively over HTTPS. All HTTP (non-TLS) connections are rejected.
Line 141: > • **API Versioning:** The API is versioned via the URI path (e.g., \`/v1/\`, \`/v2/\`). When a new API version is released, the prior version enters a deprecation period. Meridian provides a minimum of twelve (12) months of continued support for deprecated API versions following issuance of a formal sunset notice, giving customers adequate time to migrate their integrations to the current version.
Line 145: All API requests must be authenticated and authorized before processing. MeridianIQ implements industry-standard OAuth 2.0 for API authentication and fine-grained scope-based authorization.
Line 161: > • \`models:manage\` --- View and manage adapter configurations, including listing adapters and retrieving adapter performance metrics.
Line 169: The following table summarizes the core API endpoints available in MeridianIQ API v2. Detailed endpoint documentation, including request/response schemas, parameter descriptions, error codes, and example payloads, is provided in the MeridianIQ API Developer Guide, which is furnished to customers during onboarding.
Line 184:   \`/models/adapters\`                        GET                     List all adapter configurations available to the tenant, including adapter identifiers, version numbers, associated document classes, and training dates.
Line 186:   \`/models/adapters/{adapter_id}/metrics\`   GET                     Retrieve performance metrics for a specific adapter, including F1 score, precision, recall, and throughput statistics from the most recent evaluation cycle.
Line 188:   \`/health\`                                 GET                     Platform health and status check endpoint. Returns the current operational status of the API, inference pipeline, and dependent services. Suitable for integration into customer health monitoring and alerting systems.
Line 193: To ensure consistent performance and fair resource allocation across all tenants, MeridianIQ enforces the following rate limits on API requests:
Line 195: > • **Standard Tier Rate Limit:** 500 requests per second per tenant. This limit applies to all API endpoints in aggregate.
Line 199: > • **Rate Limit Response Headers:** Every API response includes the following headers to enable client-side rate limit awareness and management:
Line 207: > • **Rate Limit Exceeded Behavior:** When a tenant exceeds the applicable rate limit (including burst allowance), the API returns an HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) response. The response includes a \`Retry-After\` header indicating the number of seconds the client should wait before retrying the request. Clients are expected to implement appropriate backoff logic in their integration code to handle rate limit responses gracefully.
Line 213: The following specifications govern the size, format, and content constraints for API request and response payloads:
Line 227: > • Confidence scores: a numeric value between 0.00 and 1.00 for each extracted field, representing the model\'s confidence in the accuracy of the extracted value.
Line 231: > • Processing metadata: timestamps, processing duration, model version, adapter version, and pipeline stage details.
Line 235: **Webhook Configuration.** Customers configure one or more webhook endpoint URLs via the administrative console or the \`/admin/webhooks\` API endpoint. Webhook endpoints must be HTTPS and must respond with an HTTP 2xx status code to acknowledge receipt of the webhook payload.
Line 247: Meridian commits to maintaining a monthly uptime percentage of at least 99.9% for the MeridianIQ API, as measured and calculated in accordance with the methodology described below.
Line 253: **Downtime Definition.** \"Downtime\" is defined as any period of five (5) or more consecutive minutes during which the MeridianIQ API returns HTTP 5xx server error responses or is unreachable (i.e., fails to respond to properly formed requests) as measured by Meridian\'s external synthetic monitoring system. Meridian\'s synthetic monitoring agents issue health check requests to the API from geographically distributed external monitoring points at one-minute intervals. Intermittent errors lasting less than five consecutive minutes, or isolated request failures that do not constitute a sustained outage, are not counted as Downtime.
Line 261: > • **Customer-Caused Downtime:** Unavailability or errors resulting from the customer\'s systems, networks, code, configurations, or actions, including misconfigured API calls, exhausted rate limits, expired authentication tokens, or customer-side network outages.
Line 267: Meridian targets a 95th percentile (p95) end-to-end response latency of six hundred (600) milliseconds or less for synchronous single-document extraction API calls, measured from the MeridianIQ API gateway\'s receipt of the inbound request to the dispatch of the response from the API gateway.
Line 269: This published standard SLA parameter of p95 ≤ 600 ms establishes the vendor\'s baseline capability for production inference workloads across all supported document classes. It reflects the performance characteristics of the inference pipeline under typical production conditions, including document classification, extraction via the base model and adapter, post-processing, and response serialization.
Line 271: **Measurement Basis.** The latency target applies to synchronous single-document extraction calls (i.e., requests to the \`/documents\` endpoint processed in synchronous mode). Batch processing jobs submitted via the \`/batch\` endpoint are excluded from the latency target, as batch jobs are processed asynchronously and are subject to different throughput and scheduling dynamics.
Line 273: **Measurement Point.** Latency is measured at Meridian\'s API gateway---specifically, from the timestamp of request ingress at the gateway to the timestamp of response egress from the gateway. matches.line: MeridianIQ addresses a critical operational bottleneck in the mortgage lifecycle: the manual review, indexing, and data entry associated with the high volume and wide variety of documents generated during loan origination, underwriting, and closing. By automating these processes at the model level, MeridianIQ enables customers to reduce processing time, improve data accuracy, and free human reviewers to focus on exception handling and quality assurance rather than routine data extraction tasks.

The platform\'s target customer profile includes mortgage lenders, loan servicers, fintech platforms, and banks requiring high-throughput document intelligence at scale. MeridianIQ is designed to integrate seamlessly into existing loan origination systems (LOS), point-of-sale platforms, and servicing technologies via a well-documented RESTful API, enabling customers to embed intelligent document processing directly into their production workflows without disrupting existing system architectures.

Additional document classes beyond the standard set listed above are available through customer-specific fine-tuning engagements. During the implementation phase, Meridian works with the customer to identify additional document types relevant to the customer\'s workflows and trains custom adapter layers to support extraction from those formats. Common examples of customer-specific document classes include bank statements, asset verification letters, flood certifications, homeowners insurance declarations pages, and investor-specific stacking order checklists.

**Structured JSON Output for Downstream Integration.** All extraction results, classification labels, confidence scores, reconciliation findings, and compliance flags are returned in a structured JSON format designed for direct consumption by downstream systems such as loan origination systems, data warehouses, underwriting engines, and quality control platforms. The JSON schema is fully documented and versioned, and Meridian provides schema migration guidance when breaking changes are introduced in new API versions.

**Fine-Tuning Framework.** MeridianIQ employs a modular adapter layer architecture based on Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) principles. This approach enables customer-specific customization without modifying the underlying base model weights. During the implementation engagement, Meridian trains adapter layers on customer-provided labeled document sets to adapt the model\'s extraction behavior to the customer\'s specific document formats, terminology, field naming conventions, and extraction schemas. Because the base model weights remain frozen during adapter training, this approach is computationally efficient, preserves the base model\'s generalized document understanding capabilities, and ensures that customer-specific customizations do not interfere with other tenants\' adapter configurations.

**Adapter Layer Architecture.** Each customer\'s adapter weights are stored independently and applied dynamically at inference time. When a document is submitted for processing, the inference pipeline identifies the appropriate tenant and loads the corresponding adapter weights atop the frozen base model. This design allows Meridian to maintain a single base model version across all tenants while delivering customer-specific extraction performance. Adapter weights are versioned, and customers can maintain multiple adapter versions (e.g., for A/B testing or staged rollouts) simultaneously.
1\. **Document Ingestion:** The submitted document file is received via the API, validated for format and size compliance, and queued for processing.

4\. **Extraction via Base Model + Adapter:** The classified document is processed by the base model with the tenant\'s applicable adapter weights loaded, producing raw extraction outputs for each target field in the document class schema.

6\. **Structured Output:** The final extraction results, classification label, confidence scores, reconciliation findings, and compliance flags are assembled into the structured JSON response payload and returned to the customer via the API or webhook callback.

**2.2.1 Multi-Tenant SaaS (Standard).** The standard deployment option hosts the customer\'s workloads on shared compute infrastructure with logical tenant isolation enforced at every layer of the stack. Data segregation is maintained at the application layer (tenant-scoped API authentication and authorization), the storage layer (tenant-partitioned database schemas and isolated object storage buckets), and the network layer (security group and network policy enforcement). Each tenant\'s adapter weights are stored in isolated, encrypted object storage containers that are accessible only by the inference pipeline processes operating on behalf of that specific tenant.

The dedicated instance option is available at additional cost; pricing is determined based on the customer\'s throughput requirements, compute resource allocation, storage volume, and support tier, and is provided upon request. Dedicated instances also support enhanced security configurations including customer-managed encryption keys (CMK), mutual TLS (mTLS) for API authentication, and private network connectivity via AWS PrivateLink.

**Primary Region:** US East (N. Virginia) --- \`us-east-1\`. The primary region hosts all production workloads under normal operating conditions, including the API gateway, inference fleet, database tier, object storage, and supporting microservices.

**Auto-Scaling Inference Fleet.** The GPU-accelerated inference fleet is configured with auto-scaling policies that dynamically adjust compute capacity based on real-time demand signals including request queue depth, GPU utilization, and latency metrics. A minimum baseline capacity is reserved per tenant to ensure consistent performance during traffic spikes and to prevent resource contention between tenants on the multi-tenant deployment.

**Load Balancing.** Incoming API traffic is distributed across the inference fleet via AWS Application Load Balancer (ALB) with health-check-based routing. The ALB continuously monitors the health of backend inference instances and automatically removes unhealthy instances from the target group, redistributing traffic to healthy instances without interruption to the customer.

**Continuous Replication.** All tenant data---including processed documents, extraction results, configuration data, and adapter weights---is continuously replicated from the primary region (\`us-east-1\`) to the failover region (\`us-west-2\`). Replication is performed at both the database level (Aurora cross-region replication) and the object storage level (S3 cross-region replication), ensuring that the failover region maintains a near-real-time copy of all critical data.

**Backup Retention.** Database snapshots are retained on a 30-day rolling basis, providing point-in-time recovery capability for the most recent 30-day window. Object storage items---including adapter weights, pipeline artifacts, and processed document outputs---are retained for 90 days in both the primary and failover regions. Backup encryption is consistent with the platform\'s data-at-rest encryption standards described in Section 6.1.

**4.1 General.** MeridianIQ exposes a RESTful HTTPS API as the primary interface for all document submission, processing, extraction retrieval, and platform management operations. The API is designed to be intuitive for developers familiar with modern REST conventions and follows consistent patterns across all endpoints.
> • **Protocol:** RESTful API served exclusively over HTTPS. All HTTP (non-TLS) connections are rejected.

> • **API Versioning:** The API is versioned via the URI path (e.g., \`/v1/\`, \`/v2/\`). When a new API version is released, the prior version enters a deprecation period. Meridian provides a minimum of twelve (12) months of continued support for deprecated API versions following issuance of a formal sunset notice, giving customers adequate time to migrate their integrations to the current version.
All API requests must be authenticated and authorized before processing. MeridianIQ implements industry-standard OAuth 2.0 for API authentication and fine-grained scope-based authorization.
> • \`models:manage\` --- View and manage adapter configurations, including listing adapters and retrieving adapter performance metrics.

\`/health\`                                 GET                     Platform health and status check endpoint. Returns the current operational status of the API, inference pipeline, and dependent services. Suitable for integration into customer health monitoring and alerting systems.
To ensure consistent performance and fair resource allocation across all tenants, MeridianIQ enforces the following rate limits on API requests:
> • **Standard Tier Rate Limit:** 500 requests per second per tenant. This limit applies to all API endpoints in aggregate.
> • **Rate Limit Response Headers:** Every API response includes the following headers to enable client-side rate limit awareness and management:

> • **Rate Limit Exceeded Behavior:** When a tenant exceeds the applicable rate limit (including burst allowance), the API returns an HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) response. The response includes a \`Retry-After\` header indicating the number of seconds the client should wait before retrying the request. Clients are expected to implement appropriate backoff logic in their integration code to handle rate limit responses gracefully.
The following specifications govern the size, format, and content constraints for API request and response payloads:
> • Confidence scores: a numeric value between 0.00 and 1.00 for each extracted field, representing the model\'s confidence in the accuracy of the extracted value.

**Webhook Configuration.** Customers configure one or more webhook endpoint URLs via the administrative console or the \`/admin/webhooks\` API endpoint. Webhook endpoints must be HTTPS and must respond with an HTTP 2xx status code to acknowledge receipt of the webhook payload.
Meridian commits to maintaining a monthly uptime percentage of at least 99.9% for the MeridianIQ API, as measured and calculated in accordance with the methodology described below.

**Downtime Definition.** \"Downtime\" is defined as any period of five (5) or more consecutive minutes during which the MeridianIQ API returns HTTP 5xx server error responses or is unreachable (i.e., fails to respond to properly formed requests) as measured by Meridian\'s external synthetic monitoring system. Meridian\'s synthetic monitoring agents issue health check requests to the API from geographically distributed external monitoring points at one-minute intervals. Intermittent errors lasting less than five consecutive minutes, or isolated request failures that do not constitute a sustained outage, are not counted as Downtime.

> • **Customer-Caused Downtime:** Unavailability or errors resulting from the customer\'s systems, networks, code, configurations, or actions, including misconfigured API calls, exhausted rate limits, expired authentication tokens, or customer-side network outages.

Meridian targets a 95th percentile (p95) end-to-end response latency of six hundred (600) milliseconds or less for synchronous single-document extraction API calls, measured from the MeridianIQ API gateway\'s receipt of the inbound request to the dispatch of the response from the API gateway.

This published standard SLA parameter of p95 ≤ 600 ms establishes the vendor\'s baseline capability for production inference workloads across all supported document classes. It reflects the performance characteristics of the inference pipeline under typical production conditions, including document classification, extraction via the base model and adapter, post-processing, and response serialization.

**Measurement Basis.** The latency target applies to synchronous single-document extraction calls (i.e., requests to the \`/documents\` endpoint processed in synchronous mode). Batch processing jobs submitted via the \`/batch\` endpoint are excluded from the latency target, as batch jobs are processed asynchronously and are subject to different throughput and scheduling dynamics.

**Measurement Point.** Latency is measured at Meridian\'s API gateway---specifically, from the timestamp of request ingress at the gateway to the timestamp of response egress from the gateway. This measurement excludes network transit time between the customer\'s systems and Meridian\'s API endpoint, as network latency is influenced by factors outside Meridian\'s control, including the customer\'s geographic location, network provider, and internet routing conditions.

**Real-Time Metrics Dashboard.** A web-based metrics dashboard is accessible via the MeridianIQ console and programmatically via the \`/metrics\` API endpoint. The dashboard provides near-real-time views of the following metrics:
> • Adapter accuracy scores (F1, precision, recall by adapter and document class)

**Telemetry Export.** For customers who wish to integrate MeridianIQ metrics into their existing observability stacks (e.g., Datadog, Splunk, Grafana, New Relic), Meridian supports telemetry export via OpenTelemetry-compatible protocols. Customers can configure telemetry export to forward metrics, traces, and logs from the MeridianIQ platform to their preferred observability platform for unified monitoring and correlation with metrics from other systems in their technology ecosystem.

**Alerting.** Meridian provides configurable threshold-based alerting to notify customers when key metrics exceed or fall below customer-defined thresholds. Alerts can be delivered via email, webhook callback, or PagerDuty integration, enabling integration into the customer\'s existing incident management workflows. Common alert configurations include latency threshold breaches, elevated error rates, processing queue depth increases, and adapter accuracy degradation.

**Phase 1: Kickoff and Requirements Gathering (Weeks 1--2).** The implementation engagement begins with a formal kickoff meeting attended by stakeholders from both Meridian and the customer. During this phase, Meridian\'s implementation team works with the customer to document detailed requirements, including the target document classes, extraction field schemas, integration architecture, throughput expectations, accuracy requirements, and compliance considerations. The output of this phase is a finalized requirements document and an updated project plan with milestones and acceptance criteria.

**Phase 2: Environment Provisioning and API Integration (Weeks 3--5).** Meridian provisions the customer\'s production and sandbox environments, configures tenant settings (authentication credentials, rate limits, retention policies, webhook endpoints), and provides the customer\'s development team with API access, SDK packages, documentation, and sample code. The customer\'s development team begins API integration work during this phase, building the connectivity between the customer\'s platform and the MeridianIQ API.

**Phase 3: Adapter Fine-Tuning (Weeks 4--8).** Overlapping with Phase 2, Meridian\'s machine learning engineering team trains customer-specific adapter layers using the labeled document sets provided by the customer. This phase includes data ingestion and quality validation, adapter training runs, iterative performance evaluation against the customer\'s validation set, and hyperparameter optimization to maximize extraction accuracy on the customer\'s specific document formats. Multiple training iterations are typically required to achieve target accuracy levels, and Meridian provides regular progress updates and accuracy metrics throughout the training process.

**Phase 4: User Acceptance Testing and Validation (Weeks 9--10).** The customer conducts user acceptance testing (UAT) using the fully trained adapters and the completed API integration. The customer executes test cases against a representative set of documents to validate extraction accuracy, integration correctness, end-to-end latency, error handling, and compliance flag behavior. Meridian\'s implementation team provides support during UAT, including defect triage, adapter retraining if needed, and integration troubleshooting.

**Labeled Document Samples.** The customer is responsible for providing representative labeled document samples for adapter training. Meridian recommends a minimum of five thousand (5,000) labeled documents per document class to achieve optimal adapter accuracy. Labeled documents should be representative of the full range of document formats, layouts, print qualities, and data distributions encountered in the customer\'s production environment. Meridian provides labeling guidelines, schema templates, and quality assurance feedback during the data preparation process.

**API Integration Development.** The customer is responsible for developing and maintaining the API integration between the customer\'s platform and the MeridianIQ API, including authentication, document submission, result retrieval, webhook handling, error handling, and retry logic. Meridian provides SDKs, sample code, documentation, and integration support, but the customer retains responsibility for the design, development, testing, and deployment of the integration within the customer\'s own systems.

**User Acceptance Testing.** The customer is responsible for designing and executing user acceptance test cases that validate the MeridianIQ deployment against the customer\'s business requirements. Test cases should cover extraction accuracy across all target document classes, integration correctness, latency performance, error handling, and any customer-specific business rules or compliance requirements.

**Level 1: Meridian Support Engineering.** Initial triage and response for all support requests. Support Engineers are trained on the MeridianIQ platform and common integration patterns, and are equipped to resolve the majority of reported issues, including API connectivity problems, authentication errors, configuration questions, and standard troubleshooting.

**Level 2: Meridian Platform Engineering.** Issues that require deeper technical investigation---including suspected platform defects, performance anomalies, infrastructure-level issues, and adapter accuracy degradation---are escalated to the Platform Engineering team. Platform Engineers have direct access to the platform\'s internal systems, logs, and monitoring tools and work collaboratively with the customer and the Support Engineering team to diagnose and resolve complex issues.

These parameters may be modified, supplemented, or superseded by the specific terms of an executed customer agreement, Order Form, Statement of Work, or other binding contractual document between Meridian and the customer. 51: **2.2 --- Summary Decision Matrix**
52: 
53: The following table provides a summary-level decision matrix for each major term category addressed in this Playbook. Detailed negotiation guidance, including specific thresholds, examples, and fallback positions, is set forth in the referenced sections.
